He is reported to have resigned following the arrest of Mikhail Khodorkovsky, Russia's richest businessman. Mikhail Khodorkovsky was arrested on tax evasion charges on Sunday. On Thursday, 44 percent of the shares of Khodorkovsky's oil company Yukos were frozen, which also led to the departure of Alexander Voloshin. The shares of UCOSE were sold under the laws for the prevention of organized crime. Conflict reporters say the crackdown on Yukos is the result of a battle for supremacy between radicals and liberals. Voloshin, 47, is believed to be a supporter of liberals and businessmen and sympathizes with Khodorkovsky and his oil business. He was one of the most important officials in the Russian government under Boris Yeltsin. It is being said that Dmitry Medvedev, who is considered very close to President Putin, is now being appointed to the chair of Voloshin. Alexander Voloshin told the BBC some time ago that he considered Medvedev to be the most sensible member of the Russian government.

On Friday, Israel lifted some travel restrictions to allow Palestinian lawmakers to attend a parliamentary meeting in the West Bank city of Ramallah. After the party's decision, now Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu can call a session of the assembly in a few days to recommend to the governor to dissolve the assembly. There have been reports for quite some time that Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu is considering early elections in the state after being attacked by Maoist rebels. Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu had also held several rounds of consultations with his senior colleagues and several leaders had agreed to hold early elections. However, the opposition parties in the state, the Congress, have been opposing it. Security has also been tightened in the southern city of Basra following Wednesday's suicide attack on an Italian police base in Nasiriyah. Now, even if you don't know Japanese, you'll be able to easily'interact'with Japanese in Japan. That is, you will be able to explain your point to them and understand their point. But how? This will be possible through a robot. In Japan, a robot has now been created that will be able to translate from English to Japanese or from Japanese to English in an instant. And the amazing thing is that he will also be able to speak both languages. The technology has been developed by NEC Corporation, a major company in Japan and Europe, after years of research. It was then tried out in a robot named'Pepero '. Peppero is an all-hearing and all-seeing robot that can also communicate. Now Japan will make it available at the country's major airports under its scheme called e-Airports and thereafter Japanese airports will become the most technologically advanced airports in the world. All the tourist has to do is hire the services of'Peppero'robots as soon as they land at the airport and then a lot of difficulties will be just as easy. The robot is reported to have a vocabulary of about 50,000 Japanese and 25,000 English words.

Expressing his displeasure in a television broadcast, Arafat flatly refused to accept the plan. Under the plan, Israel wants to maintain Jewish settlements in the Gaza Strip and parts of the West Bank despite the withdrawal of its troops. It also says that Palestinians who have left their homes in Israel will not be allowed to return to their homes. About 90,000 Jews live in the six West Bank ghettos. Yasser Arafat has said that his people will continue to struggle to realize their dream of independence at all costs. Some other prominent Palestinian leaders have appealed to Arab nations and the European Union to support the International Roadmap for Peace plan. Meanwhile, US President George W. Bush is being criticized around the world for supporting Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon's controversial Middle East plan. UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan has said that President Bush's support appears to be an attempt to stop talks between Israelis and Palestinians. He said any lasting peace agreement should be based on negotiations between the two sides under the Security Council resolutions. Palestinian Prime Minister Ahmad Qura'i has also voiced his reservations about Bush's support for Sharon's plan. They say President Bush is violating his jurisdiction and could affect peace in the region as a whole. "When President Bush said that the 1967 borders could not be returned, he became the first (US) president to legalise settlements on Palestinian territory," Quraishi said. "" Sharon's plan has also been welcomed by British Prime Minister Tony Blair, but he has been a bit cautious. "" " He says the plan is a step towards broader peace. Palestinian negotiator and minister Saeb Arakat also criticized the United States, saying the plan violates UN resolutions. Policy change observers see Bush's support for Israel as a sign of a significant shift in America's long-standing policy. US President George W Bush has said that the long-standing problem can be solved if all sides take advantage of this opportunity. Ariel Sharon is currently on a visit to the United States, and on Wednesday, President Bush patted Sharon on the back over his controversial plan in Sharon's presence. Bush called the plan bold and historic. According to observers, President Bush has ignored the Palestinians'view that the new state should be formed after negotiations keeping in mind the 1967 borders. Israel occupied the West Bank and Gaza Strip in 1967.

The Border Security Force has sealed the 865-kilometre-long India-Bangladesh international border and large-scale additional forces have been deployed in view of the recent militant attacks. In addition, four IAF aircraft have been patrolling militant-affected and sensitive areas since yesterday. State Chief Election Commissioner K V Satyanarayana told reporters that "elaborate security arrangements have been made across the state and adequate number of Assam Rifles, Border Security Force, Tripura State Rifles and state police personnel have been deployed for the purpose." In the past, the outfit had shot dead four Border Security Force (BSF) personnel and injured two others. Of the total 2,372 polling stations in the state, 150 are in the All Tripura Tiger Force affected area of West Tripura district. Special security arrangements have been made in the wake of the election boycott announcement and special surveillance is being carried out in sensitive areas with the help of additional security forces. When asked about this, Election Commissioner Satyanarayanan said, "It has been the tradition of Tripura to vote in large numbers irrespective of such threats." He informed that in view of the Lok Sabha elections, elaborate and unprecedented security arrangements have been made and nobody will be allowed to influence the election process in the state. The Election Commission has appointed eight central observers to oversee the polling, which is scheduled to be held here on 22nd. Tripura has two Lok Sabha seats which were held by Communist Party of India-Marxist candidates in the last elections. Tripura has about 2 million voters, of which about 50 percent are women. In this election, 6 candidates each are trying their luck from both the Lok Sabha seats. In Tripura, Communist Party candidates have won the Lok Sabha elections about 8 to 9 times since 1952. The party's candidates are said to be in a strong position in this election as well. According to poll analysts, the main contest here will be between the Communist Party of India-Marxist and the BJP-Trinamil Nadu combine, with the Congress projected to finish third.

These targets were to be met by 2015. But now the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund have released a joint report that comments on the performance of developing countries. These goals were named the "Millennium Development Goals." Some of the key goals were to halve the number of extremely poor people, provide primary education to all children, and reduce the number of maternal and child deaths during childbirth. In order to meet these goals, it is essential that the rich countries and their commitments to economic cooperation made two years ago are met, the report said. World Bank chief James T. Wolfensohn has said, "We can make as much as we want, but we will be far from the goal unless we face the fundamental question." Earlier on Wednesday, the World Economic Forum had also published its report which had some similar points as reported by the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund. The report will now be discussed at a ministerial meeting in Washington this weekend.

More than 90 people, including 29 candidates, have died during the campaign. All presidential candidates gathered on Sunday to pray for a peaceful vote, amid insurgent attacks and threats of vote rigging. Around 230,000 security personnel have been deployed in polling booths across the country. However, some new violent incidents have been reported before the polling began. Two people were killed by unidentified gunmen at a candidate's headquarters in Manila in the latest violence, a police official told AFP news agency. There are also reports of abductions of aides of local candidates and a fire caused by a blast in the East Samar district. Polls ahead of the election show Philippines President Gloria Arroyo ahead of rival film star Fernando Poe Jr. President Arroyo is being seen as the leading contender for the office. A recent poll by research company Pulse Asia estimated that Arroyo would receive 37 per cent of the vote, compared to 31 per cent for star Fernando Jr. The other three presidential contenders are former education secretary Raul Rocco, former police chief Panfilo Luxson, and evangelist Eduardo Villenua. It is estimated that the remaining one-third of the votes will be split between them. The main issues observers believe are the major issues in the Philippines, the declining economy, rising debt, Islamic extremism, and communist extremism. Corruption is also emerging as a major problem. The Reuters news agency has quoted some sources as saying that money has also been given to several bahubalis to garner votes for 17,000 local and government positions.

His elder brother Mian Nawaz Sharif has been prime minister of Pakistan twice and was removed from power in October 1999 by then army chief Pervez Musharraf. Shehbaz Sharif started his career in politics with being elected as a member of the Punjab Legislative Assembly in 1993 and he remained a member till 1996. He quickly built up the image of an able and efficient Speaker of the Legislative Assembly, becoming Chief Minister in 1997 and holding the post until 1999. Fans of Shehbaz Sharif say he provided a lot of infrastructure during his tenure, including many new roads and bridges. Shehbaz Sharif is also credited with many reforms in the state civil service of Punjab. But critics of Shehbaz Sharif say much has gone wrong during his tenure. He is alleged to have ordered the killing of five suspected criminals in police custody in 1998. In July last year, a Pakistani anti-terrorism court declared him wanted and absconding in that case. Shahbaz Sharif's supporters say that after Nawaz Sharif was expelled from the country in 2000, he too was left with no option but to leave the country. But the government says Shehbaz, along with the entire Sharif family, left the country with the promise that they would not return to the country again for ten years.

The Congress-led United Progressive Alliance (UPA) has drawn up a common minimum programme to run the government that the Left parties are considering on Wednesday. Other coalition partners are also due to give their suggestions for consideration on Wednesday, with a formal announcement expected on Thursday. AB Bardhan told reporters in Delhi today that his party wants some of his suggestions to be included in the Common Minimum Programme. Notably, the Left parties have some differences with the Congress on economic policies on which any consensus is being sought. The Congress is in favour of liberalisation, while the Left parties have said that public sector companies running for profit or which can be profited from should not be disinvested. However, after the Communist Party of India-Marxist agreed to accept the post of Lok Sabha Speaker, it is being speculated that it will ensure support for the stability of the government. The Congress had offered to make CPI (M) leader Somnath Chatterjee the Lok Sabha Speaker, which has been accepted.

But Israel has called the decision unfair, saying it will not accept the International Court of Justice's ruling, which is also not binding. Several countries, including the United States and Britain, have asked the International Court of Justice to stay away from the case as it would hamper Middle East peace planning. White House spokesman Scott McClellan said, "We don't think it's an appropriate forum to address a political problem." The International Court of Justice ruling could provide the basis for the United Nations to make a decision. The Chinese judge ruled that the construction of such a wall was a violation of international humanitarian law. According to the court, such a wall could later become the boundary between the two countries in the event of the Palestinians becoming a separate nation. The court also called Israeli settlements in the Palestinian territories a violation of international rules. Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat welcomed the court's decision, saying it was a victory for Palestinians and free people around the world.

Chidambaram said he was also ready for the Left parties to satisfy him on their side. The Left parties are quite angry with the proposal and have decided to oppose it in Parliament as well. Congress spokesperson Anand Sharma briefed the meeting of UPA MPs and said the Left parties were also not in favour of over-riding the FDI issue and had no intention of confrontation with the government.

He became the world number 73, also reaching the third round of the US Open. The pair, popularly known as the Indian Express, also became the number one pair in the world. But Paes's teammate Mahesh Bhupathi also remembers his medal at the Olympics first. "When Leander won the Olympic berth, I was there, watching the match," says Mahesh Bhupathi. It was indeed a proud moment for the country. This is the dream of every athlete. "Many professional tennis players in the world still do not value the Olympics. Russia's Marat Safin says tennis doesn't need the Olympics. General Pervez Musharraf expressed this hope during his meeting with Indian Foreign Minister Natwar Singh in Rawalpindi on Friday. Natwar Singh had gone to Pakistan to attend a meeting of SAARC countries and left for India on Friday after a nearly one-and-a-half-hour meeting with General Pervez Musharraf. Before leaving for India, Natwar Singh said at the Islamabad airport, "During this meeting, there was no issue left which was not discussed, including Jammu and Kashmir." "In this meeting, we discussed different aspects on different issues. Satisfaction was also expressed at the ongoing government-to-government dialogue. "Natwar Singh said that India and Pakistan are committed to dialogue and resolution of all issues, including Jammu and Kashmir, in a manner that satisfies both countries." During his visit, Natwar Singh also met Pakistan Prime Minister Shujaat Hussain and Foreign Minister Khurshid Mahmud Kasuri and reviewed the ongoing peace process between the two countries. Prime Minister Shujaat Hussain has said that Pakistan will make every effort to improve relations with India. Musharraf had also said on Thursday night that no concrete progress could be made on improving relations with India unless the Kashmir issue was resolved, news agency PTI reported. "We are working on ways to advance dialogue and enhance understanding with India, but Kashmir is the core issue that needs to be resolved," Musharraf was quoted as saying by PTI. "" Unless concrete progress is made to resolve this issue, there cannot be concrete progress in enhancing mutual understanding in other areas. "" "

About two-thirds of the country is affected by floods. Even half of the capital Dhaka has been flooded. The slum areas have been under the grip of floods for several days. Dirty drains have also been flooded and thousands of people have had to be hospitalized with complaints of diarrhoea. In some southern areas of Dhaka, the water level has risen to levels never seen before. Floods in Bangladesh have so far killed at least 200 people. These people have died due to drowning, electrocution, and snakebites. Residents of Dhaka are taking measures to avoid flood waters. Wherever the water from the banks of the rivers is filling up the residential areas, people are engaged in rescue by throwing sandbags. Although the water level of the Ganges and Meghna rivers in India has begun to fall, the Met department predicts more rain in the coming days.

By taking regular courses, such people are coming forward to become professional astrologers who find it a little difficult to call Panditji or Shastriji. From generation to generation, this traditional form of study, driven by the guru-shishya tradition, is changing rapidly, computers have replaced the booklet and the Chutia Pandit has been replaced by English-speaking youths wearing jeans. About twenty-five universities in India offer degrees in astrology after formal studies, which have seen a huge influx of enrollees these days. S Ganesh, a professor of astrology at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan in Delhi, believes that "when people can take up subjects like cooking and home decor as a profession, why not astrology?" Regarding the ever-growing belief in astrology, Ila Shukla, daughter of a famous astrologer, says that "life is no longer as simple as it used to be. In this age of stress and competition, astrology is helping to ease life to some extent, so its popularity is increasing. "Says Sheela Parkhi, an astrology student," It is a respectable profession, with a lot of money, and it can be done sitting at home, providing ideal opportunities for women. "Till a few years ago, the number of astrologers in Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan was 50 to 100, but this year it has increased to 800. Explaining the reason for the increase in the number of people reading this subject, S. Ganesh says, "Earlier only people of a particular caste used to study it, but now the doors of astrology have been opened to everyone." But there are people who believe that opening the doors to everyone does not mean that all will become good astrologers. Ajay Jha, who prophesies by looking at his hands in front of the famous Hanuman temple in Delhi, says that ninety percent experience and sadhana is required in this profession. Claiming to be directly connected to God, he says "If the knowledge of astrology comes only by reading, then not all become astrologers." In astrology, the voice of the soul plays a major role and is possible only through sadhana. "Although computers are now being used for prediction, experts in this field believe that a slight error anywhere can give wrong predictions. The predictions of the astrologers may be right or wrong, but a prediction can be made without fail that the face of the astrologers and astrologers will change completely in the coming time.

Subir Bhowmick, a BBC correspondent from Kolkata, says families with underage girls have particularly welcomed the decision. Tamal and Shubhra Mukherjee, who have two school-going daughters, say the President's decision is commendable and welcome. He believes that Dhananjay should have been hanged much earlier, his wife also agrees with him and says that the death penalty is necessary to prevent other criminals from committing the crime. Jhanvi Biswas, a housewife from Kolkata, says that "there is nothing wrong with the death penalty, other methods like shooting can be adopted if people object to the method of hanging." Most of those who spoke to the BBC believed that crimes against women should not be tolerated at all. West Bengal was considered quite safe for women until a few years ago, but like other parts of the country, incidents of rape and murder are on the rise. State Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee said it was right that a heinous criminal like Dhananjay should be hanged to death for instilling fear in criminals. Many of us who oppose the complete abolition of the death penalty are also unhappy with this decision of the President. Renowned film actress and editor of a women's magazine Aparna Sen believes that the death penalty for Dhananjay will not do anything, the death penalty has not been effective in stopping crime in any country. Aparna Sen's view has also been endorsed by the APDR, a Kolkata-based human rights organisation. Activists of the organisation protested and raised slogans in Kolkata against the President's decision. APDR general secretary Sujato Bhadra says that "our organisation is not against punishing criminals but against the death penalty, especially the death penalty." After the President's latest decision, it seems that Dhananjay Chatterjee, who has been found guilty of rape and murder, is almost certain to be hanged.

Al-Jazeera television channel has said that a video it received showed the death of Italian journalist Enzo Baldoni. Al-Jazeera says an organisation called the Islamic Army in Iraq has said it killed Baldoni because Italy is not willing to withdraw its troops from Iraq. Notably, Al-Jazeera aired on Tuesday the hijackers'threat that Baldoni's safety would not be guaranteed if Italy did not withdraw its troops from Iraq within 48 hours. The Italian government had said it would make every effort to secure the journalist's release, but it had no intention of withdrawing troops from Iraq. Italy has 3,000 troops in Iraq. Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi has condemned the killing of the Italian journalist. Baldoni had been missing since August 19. Earlier, the body of his Iraqi driver was found in Najaf. Baldoni, 56, who works for a Milanese magazine, was also active as an activist for the Red Cross in Iraq.

Dr Singh has also proposed India's bid for membership of the UN Security Council. Referring to the ongoing dialogue with Pakistan, the Prime Minister said India is committed to a meaningful dialogue with Pakistan on all issues, including Jammu and Kashmir. It is also being seen as a response to Pakistan President Pervez Musharraf's soft stance adopted at the UN General Assembly. "India and Pakistan have initiated a comprehensive dialogue to resolve all issues, including Kashmir," Manmohan Singh said. I want to assure you that we would like to take this dialogue to an acceptable and objective conclusion. He has stressed the need for an international fight against terrorism. Dr Singh said the fight against terrorism needs to be made truly credible and leave double standards for political gains. In his speech, Manmohan Singh also pitched for a permanent seat on the UN Security Council. Officials say the government has directed the police to provide safe passage to the three prominent Maoist leaders. Police officers will speak to PWG mediators Vara Vara Rao, Gadar and Kalyan Rao about the security of the interlocutors. Murray has said he sent a tip-off to the government claiming that a newspaper learned last week that Britain's MI-6 intelligence agency had used that tip-off. Inaugurating the Pravasi Bharatiya Divas convention in Mumbai, the Prime Minister said, "I declare to grant dual citizenship to all Indians settled abroad after 1950, provided their local law permits it." Manmohan Singh said reforms in the way NRIs register in India were also being considered. All options, including smart cards, are being studied for this, he said. Last year, the Indian Parliament approved granting dual citizenship to NRIs from 16 countries, including the US and the UK. After Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's announcement on Friday, the facility is now available to all NRIs. It is estimated that the number of Indians settled abroad is over 25 million. The Indian government wants to increase the amount of overseas Indian investment in the country. It is believed that giving dual citizenship to more and more NRIs will make this task easier. More than 1500 NRIs from 60 countries are participating in the Pravasi Bharatiya Divas Conference. The conference will last for three days. The conference will also discuss in detail the devastation caused by the recent tsunami waves in India.

This was stated by the Supreme Court while interpreting clauses three and four of section eight of the Representation of the People Act. Constitutionalist Rajeev Dhawan considers it merely a reinterpretation of the Representation of the People Act. "" "All these provisions mean that if you commit an offence in which you have been sentenced to two years or more, you will be disqualified for the next election," "he explains." Elaborating further on the Supreme Court's interpretation, Dhavan said, "If you are a member of a House at present, you will be allowed to continue till the completion of the term of the current House, but coming within the purview of this provision for the next election, you will not be eligible to contest even if you have appealed to a court of law." Experts point out that after this interpretation, tainted MLAs and MPs will no longer be able to contest elections under the guise of appeals. The reason for the interpretation is that the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court invalidated the election of Indian National Lok Dal candidate Nafe Singh in Haryana, who had won the 2000 assembly elections. Nafe Singh was elected a member of the Haryana Legislative Assembly on 10 May 1996 and was sentenced to life imprisonment by a court on 17 May 1999 for murder. The High Court had stayed Nafe Singh's conviction but only a few months later, in December 1999, the governor dissolved the assembly for mid-term elections. When Nafe Singh filed his nomination for the new elections, the Congress candidate opposed it, but the Returning Officer did not accept his argument. Now in this case, the Supreme Court has clarified this law. Arguments for abuse Following this ruling, there have also been arguments from some quarters that politicians can influence lower court decisions to spoil the political future of their opponents. However, Rajeev Dhawan does not accept this argument. "This is a two-year sentence that will now be carried out by an experienced judge in the sessions court," he explains. If there are any loopholes, it can be cleared by an appeal. "However, this arrangement will only serve to clear the matter, but since elections are around the corner in Haryana, Bihar and Jharkhand, the impact will be visible soon.

Two toy companies in Japan - Tommy and Takara - have developed a plant that can help such people. These companies have developed a semiprecious seed that transmits this particular message to another person when it germinates. The Takara company says that this plant is a new kind of message card that can convey your feelings to other people. In fact, the plant can convey six different types of messages, including "good luck" and "I love you." These messages are laser-written on this plant. The Tommy company, on the other hand, lays a white egg that contains the bean seed and when placed in the water, the egg hatches and then the seed sprouts and the message is visible. The message is written in French on one side and Japanese on the other. Both these plants will be available in the market from February.

It has been suspected that the new pope may not be as confident in doing so. His election has been met with surprise in Turkey, as he opposed Turkey's membership of the European Union, saying it would be better if Turkey gained the membership of Arab countries. Prominent among the challenges facing Pope Benedict XVI is the Vatican's attitude towards Islam. There are some Catholics who want to pursue dialogue with other denominations, following the policy of Pope John Paul II. But there are others who disagree with this view. When the new pope was in the position of cardinal, he had the role of the principal theologian and was seen as a custodian of Vatican policies. He believed that Catholics should rise above the idea that all religions were equal. His idea was to have dialogue with other religions but on the basis that Catholicism was paramount. When he opposed Turkey's membership of the European Union, the idea behind it was that there were already about 15 million Muslims in Europe, and if Turkey, a Muslim country, joined it, Europe's Christianity would be affected. Perhaps this is why his election in Turkey is criticized in almost every newspaper. One newspaper headline reads "Anti-Turkish cardinal elected pope" and another reads "The new pope is against Turkey." The new pope said that Turkey sees itself as a secular nation but that Turkey is an Islamic country. Now it remains to be seen if his attitude changes after coming to this position. If the Vatican changes its mind after September 11 in a world where there are already tensions between Islam and the West, it could have serious consequences.

In the previous parliament, the ruling Labour Party had a majority of 161 MPs. In this election, about 45 million voters could exercise their franchise to elect 645 MPs. There are a total of 646 seats in the House of Commons, the lower house of the UK Parliament, but elections were postponed in one seat due to the death of a candidate. Thus, any party would need to win 324 seats to secure a majority. The main political parties in the fray are the ruling Labour Party, the opposition Conservative Party and the Liberal Democrats. In the previous parliament, Labour had won 413 seats, the Conservatives 166 and the Liberal Democrats 52. Preliminary election results will start coming in about two hours after polling ends, but early Friday it will be clear who will form the government. Many voters had already voted by mail or used postal ballots. There were about 6 million voters who had registered their names to vote by mail. This time, activists of political parties were allowed to be present as long as the officials were checking the validity of the postal votes. Elaborate security arrangements were made in the capital, London. While the voter turnout was 78% in 1992 and 71% in 1997, it was only 59% in 2001, the lowest since 1918.

Addressing reporters, former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee said the way the government has shown speed in dissolving the Bihar assembly, the same should be shown in holding elections there. He said there should be early and fair elections. Bharatiya Janata Party president LK Advani called it a repeat of 1975 and said India had once again been sent into a state of emergency. Talking to reporters on Monday morning, Home Minister Shivraj Patil said the President has given his assent to dissolve the assembly in Bihar. At a late-night cabinet meeting on Sunday, it was decided at around 1.30 pm that the Bihar Assembly should be dissolved. The cabinet took the decision on the basis of a report by the state governor, Buta Singh, which said the only option was to dissolve the state assembly in view of the "high-speed" MLA poaching in the political activities of the past. "Governor Buta Singh told the BBC in an exclusive interview," "The MLAs were being smuggled to other states to form the government, which is wrong and that is why I recommended the dissolution of the assembly." "" This had become necessary in view of the developments of the last few days. We had no other option. "This decision of the government has also been supported by the Left. Communist Party of India leader D Raja told the BBC that the government had no choice after the political developments in the state became immoral and unconstitutional. Nitish Kumar, the JD (U) president, has rubbished the allegation. "It's all nonsense, the efforts to form the government started in the first week of April. When the Centre thought we would form the government, they called an emergency cabinet meeting and as a conspiracy, the assembly was dissolved, "he said, calling the Bihar governor the spokesperson of the central government and demanding his immediate removal. BJP Vice President Venkaiah Naidu also addressed the media in this regard and said that after this step of the government, it has become clear that the central government does not want to let a non-Congress government in any state. In Bihar, BJP workers burnt effigies of the central government and Ram Vilas Paswan at several places, including the state capital, Patna, to protest against the dissolution of the assembly. The NDA has also called for a Bihar bandh on Tuesday. What will happen next but what will happen now in the state. There is only one option left and that is elections. All the corridors of power are also acknowledging that there is no other option but to gear up for the elections. However, there is no clarity on when the elections will be held. When contacted by the BBC in Delhi, senior journalist Sankarshan Thakur said, "In view of the floods and rains in Bihar after July, there is no possibility of elections till September and I don't think the government is in a position to hold elections before July." It is too early to say anything about the new political equations in the state in the next four-eight months.

Notably, Kabir Bedi was born and brought up in Delhi and it is Delhi that has seen him rise through the tough times as a talented actor. In later days, Kabir's acting career not only took off in Mumbai Film City, but he also made his mark in the international film industry. Kabir's time in setting these acting milestones has since passed from Mumbai to various cities in Europe, but the memory of Delhi floats in his mind. In a conversation with the BBC in London, Kabir Bedi opened up about himself, his films and acting. "I am a Delhiite at heart and in fact. The memories of Delhi have always stayed with me and will remain for the rest of my life. I am very fond of Delhi cuisine because they are not only meant to be eaten but they also remind me of my childhood. "It seemed that Kabir Bedi's unique high-pitched and melodious voice was truly described by his personality without much effort. Kabir Bedi is one of the few actors from India who has made a mark internationally but is still connected to his native Delhi and wishes to return to Delhi one day. Kabir Bedi is playing the influential role of Khan Sahib in the musical For Pavilion in London's West End, which he is not only excited but satisfied about. Kabir Bedi says that the role has literally given him an opportunity to hone his acting talent, "Understand that in the role of Khan Sahib, the music is the soul of the play." Bedi believes that working in theatre is very important and very satisfying for an actor. In films, sometimes the shooting of a scene is completed and sometimes the shooting takes place in the middle of the story and there is a lot of rehearsal, so the medium is completely different. Bedi says, "There is absolutely no scope for rehearsal in the theatre and the actor has to prove his talent and ability, there is an emotional journey going on in the theatre, which gives a high level of professional satisfaction." Kabir Bedi says that in films, there are many rehearsals for a scene. There may be bar shoots but rehearsals are very important in the theatre as there is no room for error in acting in front of the audience. Taj Mahal Kabir Bedi is quite excited about the lead role of old Shah Jahan in the new film Taj Mahal and describes it as a very important character in his acting career. About his character, he said that Aurangzeb, after taking over politics, imprisoned Shah Jahan in the Agra Fort, through the window of which he used to see the Taj Mahal in his last days, and this is where he narrates his story to Jahanara. "Acting is one of the best roles of my life. If my name is associated with this character, then I will understand that I have achieved a high degree of success. "Kabir Bedi explains that his desire was to become an architect but at that time there were some circumstances in the family that even some work had to be done to pay for college. So I enrolled for a bachelor's degree in history at St. Stephen's College, Delhi, and simultaneously started working in All India Radio and Doordarshan, earning some income, explains Kabir Bedi. In addition, he continued to do theatre. When Kabir Bedi was asked what else was left for him to do, he replied that he wished to settle down in Delhi again. "The journey of my life started from Delhi and I wish to end there. I just wait for the moment when this wish comes true, only then will I consider myself perfect. "Kabir Bedi is also working in some other international films.

The G-4 comprises Brazil, Japan and Germany along with India. These countries had proposed to increase the number of members of the Security Council from 15 to 25. The United States says member states are divided on the issue. A State Department spokeswoman, Shireen Tahir Khali, said the United States would work to expand the Security Council "but in the right way at the right time." The G-4 countries introduced the proposal on Monday. That's being debated. It is not yet clear when the vote on the motion will take place. However, a two-thirds vote would be required for the resolution to pass. The G-4 countries'proposal calls for an increase of 10 more seats on the Security Council, six of which are for new permanent members. According to the proposal, the new permanent members will include African countries in addition to the G-4 countries. G-4 countries currently agree to permanent membership without the right to veto. The US stance has dealt a severe blow to the G-4 countries, which had hoped for the resolution to be passed. The issue of the inclusion of new members in the Security Council is generally agreed upon among the member states, but there are major differences on how to achieve this. The Security Council currently has 15 members, of which five are permanent members with veto power.

British Airways flights at Heathrow had been suspended since Thursday evening. The airline has said that employees who went on strike are returning to work. The current crisis began when British Airways loading and unloading staff went on a sudden strike on Thursday evening. British Airways employees went on strike to protest the dismissal of the airline's food delivery staff. This has affected 70,000 passengers to and from British Airways, and hundreds of people had to spend Thursday night at Terminal Four of the airport. Other airlines closed the doors of the terminal at the affected airport to prevent overcrowding. Because of this, many people also spent the night outside the terminal. For some passengers, British Airways provided hotel accommodation. Heathrow, the world's largest airport excluding US airports, was rocked when 600 employees of the British Airways catering company were laid off. Some regular British Airways employees also suddenly went on strike in support of him. British Airways employees who went on strike include luggage attendants, loading and unloading and other ground duty staff. The employees of the food company were fired after they refused to work with the staff on duty. No agreement was reached on the matter on Thursday, and British Airways announced it was cancelling flights until at least Friday evening. Five other airlines have also been affected by the action. These are Sri Lanka Airways, Finnair, GB Airways, British Mediterranean Airlines, and Qantas. Even for these flights, services at the airport are provided by British Airways staff.

The situation was the same in all the houses we visited one after the other. On a full afternoon, more than 50 houses were burned in the city center. The administration and the entire city watched in silence. Krishna's house appears in front of him as soon as he enters the first street. He has two young daughters, one of whom he had arranged for a wedding, which is a heap of ashes in front of him. "For my daughter's wedding, I made some jewellery and got some new clothes," says Krishna. They took everything with them, and everything else has been burned. Not even a grain left to eat. "Similarly, Roshni diligently taught her children, built a pucca house a few months before earning a living, married a son, but today she has piles of ashes in every room. His tears wouldn't stop. Not only did his grief burn everything he had, "we had left home out of fear. But they still burned down my house and, sadly, the people who burned down my house, I have served them and their parents all my life, yet they have not shown mercy to my widow. "This incident of vandalism in front of the police is not a sudden one. The biradari panchayat of 12 villages in the area, which includes only upper-caste people, carried out the act 48 hours ago by issuing an ultimatum. The administration was aware of this. But to deal with the possibility of a major mishap, the police and the local administration instead of beefing up the security of the Dalit Basti, instructed the Dalits to leave the Basti and stay out for a few days. Sohan Lal, an eyewitness, said everything happened in the presence of the police. He explains, "The police came at six in the morning, they asked all the Dalits to leave the settlement and when our houses were set on fire in the afternoon, not only the police force was present there but the higher officials were also near the place of incident." Haryana Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda said in Delhi, "The administration was apprehensive and trying to resolve the issue, but in the meantime, some mischievous elements set fire to the houses of five Dalits, which also spread to the rest of the houses." There have been several cases of atrocities against Dalits before the Gohana incident. Of these, in Haryana, the killing of five Dalits on Dussehra, the boycott of Dalits in Palwal, and now the incident in Yeh Gohana, and many more incidents that go unreported. No one guilty of any of the incidents has been punished to date. In fact, the law has always bowed to the influence of the self-styled panchayats behind such incidents, because even after 58 years, the nexus of power and feudalism is still very strong. Otherwise, what is the reason that economic reformers have been talking about social reform only on special occasions?

However, according to eyewitnesses, several innocent people have been killed in the attack. Helicopters and aircraft were used in the airstrike. One of the targets of the attack was the site of a bombing that killed five American soldiers on Saturday. The US statement said the bomb was being re-dropped, a charge local residents have denied. Conflicting reports state that an F-15 aircraft targeted the group with a laser-guided bomb, killing at least 20 militants, according to the US statement. On the other hand, the AP news agency quoted witnesses as saying that the attack was carried out on people gathered around a damaged US military vehicle, and that at least 25 people were killed in the attack. Several militants have also been killed in an attack on people firing on a helicopter in the village of Al Bufraj, according to the US statement. In another attack, US FA-18 aircraft targeted a building. According to US sources, 40 militants were killed in the attack, while the AP news agency quoted witnesses as saying that at least 14 civilians were among the dead. Remarkably, Ramadi and the surrounding region in western Iraq are considered strongholds of anti-American militants.

The UN Secretary-General has said the attacks are "shocking." Britain has said this makes it clear that extremists have no regard for human life. At the same time, France has said that such activities cannot be justified under any circumstances. There is no official word on the number of people killed in the blasts, but 60 people are reported dead and 200 injured. A high alert has been sounded following the blasts. The government has advised people to stay at home. Police are stationed outside the city's main squares and buildings. No group has so far claimed responsibility for the blasts. As many as 10 people have been arrested in this connection. The blasts come ahead of Diwali and Eid when the market is heavily crowded. Indian Prime Minister Manmohan Singh left his trip to the northeast midway and returned to Delhi. An emergency meeting of the Home Ministry has also been held. Speaking about the blasts, Minister of State for Home Affairs Sriprakash Jaiswal said such incidents will be met with a befitting reply. He said steps had also been taken to prevent it but it was a difficult task given the large size of the country. Delhi Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit has announced a compensation of Rs three lakh to the next of kin of the deceased and Rs 50,000 to the injured from the Delhi government. The first blast in Delhi occurred at 5: 30 am IST in the crowded Paharganj area. According to eyewitnesses, the Paharganj blast was very powerful and caused many casualties. Paharganj is very close to the New Delhi station and is always crowded in this street-crunch area. The second blast occurred half an hour later at around 6 pm in Sarojini Nagar. According to Paul Danhar of गई.बीबीसी, at least three people have been killed in the blast in the area. The third blast took place in a bus in south Delhi's Govindpuri area. The injured have been admitted to Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital. The leaves of the medical staff have been cancelled in view of the number of injured.

Shahabuddin, an MP from Bihar's Siwan region, was arrested by a team of Bihar Police from his MP residence in Delhi, according to PTI. Earlier, the Bihar government had issued a nationwide alert over his arrest. The Bihar police had informed all state police that there was a non-bailable warrant against Shahabuddin and that he should be arrested wherever he was seen. Notably, he was in Delhi earlier when the Bihar Police reached Delhi to arrest him and was attending the monsoon session of Parliament. But he went missing after that. However, Shahabuddin has been constantly talking to reporters in the meantime. He had said in the conversation that he was not running away from the law and had approached the court against the charges against him. Although there are eight non-bailable warrants against Shahabuddin, the case in which the police were moving with an arrest warrant against him is related to arms. Notably, the administration had asked him to hand over whatever licensed weapons he and his family had to the administration. But failing to do so, an arrest warrant was issued against him. The Bihar government was also under pressure from the Election Commission's directive that the government arrest those against whom non-bailable warrants are pending as soon as possible. Shahabuddin was jailed at the time of the last election.

According to this report, the risk of infection still remains very high for pregnant women. However, the report notes that the number of people infected with the HIV virus has increased worldwide. The report was released worldwide on Monday. In India, 51 lakh people are infected with HIV virus. According to UNAIDS, southern and western states of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Maharashtra have stabilized infection rates. But poor and densely populated northern Indian states such as Bihar and Uttar Pradesh have a much higher risk of infection among pregnant women. The report said more than one per cent of women in the industrialised states of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Maharashtra and the northeastern states of Nagaland and Manipur were found to have the AIDS virus. UNAIDS says these women are getting the virus from their husbands and are now expanding beyond urban areas. The report states that these men have AIDS caused by unprotected sex with prostitutes. According to a 2003 survey, 14% of prostitutes in Karnataka and 19% of prostitutes in Andhra Pradesh were diagnosed with AIDS. A survey conducted in Mysore found 26 per cent of prostitutes to be infected with AIDS. Of these, 14% use condoms regularly with their clients and 91% never use condoms with their husbands or partners. Benefits of Education A survey conducted in a red light area of Kolkata suggests that teaching safe sex can reduce HIV transmission. Condom use in Sonagachi has increased by 85%, reducing the rate of AIDS infection to 4% in 2004 from 11% in 2001. But since such education was not imparted in Mumbai, the infection rate among prostitutes there is still not less than 52 per cent. The report also highlights the increasing risk of AIDS among drug addicts in India, through injection and subsequent physical contact.

Presently, Cyclone FANUS lies 550 km southeast of Chennai. The meteorological department says the storm will move faster within the next 24 hours. People in coastal areas of the state have been put on alert. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea. The storm is causing winds of up to 70 kilometers per hour in coastal areas. Apart from Tamil Nadu, heavy rains are also expected in southern Andhra Pradesh due to FANUS. Chennai had received heavy rains in the same week. Several areas in Chennai were waterlogged due to heavy rains. 75,000 people were evacuated to safer areas due to the floods. More than 75,000 people had to be evacuated from their homes and placed in 140 camps due to the heavy rains.

The train service, to be called the Thar Express, will run between Munabao in Rajasthan and Khokhrapar in Pakistan and will start on 1 February 2006. The announcement was made on Friday after talks between officials of the two countries in Delhi. This will be the second rail link between the two countries. One rail link is through the Samjhauta Express which runs between the borders of Punjab in both countries. The rail link between Munabao and Khokhrapar was severed during the 1965 war and this rail service has been closed since then. India and Pakistan decided to restore this rail link in December 2004. It was earlier expected that the rail link would be operational by October 2005, then it was decided to start from 1 January 2006. However, the January 1 date was also delayed due to delays in negotiations on finalising plans for this rail link between the two countries. Due to the closure of rail service for the last 40 years, the condition of the railway tracks had deteriorated a lot and a lot of work was to be done to restore it. The Samjhauta Express was also resumed between the two countries in 2004. Tensions between the two countries escalated after the December 2001 terrorist attack on the Indian Parliament, which also affected the Samjhauta Express and led to its closure.

At the same time, India has proposed to extend the Munabao-Khokhrapar rail service to Ajmer so that pilgrims from Pakistan do not face difficulty in reaching Ajmer Sharif. The train service between Manabao and Khokhrapar is scheduled to start from February 1. India suggested that security posts should not be set up along the LoC and that a brigade commander-level flag meeting be held along the LoC. The Foreign Secretary-level talks, which began in New Delhi on Tuesday, discussed peace and security on the first day. Kashmir will be discussed on Wednesday. The Indian delegation at the two-day talks on Balochistan is led by Foreign Secretary Shyam Saran and the Pakistani delegation is led by Riyaz Mohammad Khan. India's Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Navtej Sarna said Pakistan has put forward some new suggestions to enhance mutual understanding on the nuclear issue. However, the spokesperson declined to divulge details and said these are yet to be discussed. Pakistan raised the issue of India's statement on Balochistan and considered it as an internal interference. India called it "unfounded" and said it had no intention of interfering, expressing concern only over events in the neighbourhood. India, on the other hand, expressed concern over the rising incidents of extremism. During the talks, the steps taken so far towards building trust were also reviewed and found satisfactory by both sides. It discussed rail service, bus service and opening of Line of Control at five places. Difficulties in opening consulates in Mumbai and Karachi were also discussed. The foreign secretary-level talks will continue on Wednesday and are expected to discuss drug trafficking, Siachen and Kashmir.

The Supreme Court had issued notice to Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee on the appeal of the sacked MPs and an all-party meeting was held to consider it. Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee said all parties were of the opinion that in the case of dismissal, the Speaker should neither respond to the Supreme Court notice nor appear in court. The Speaker said the BJP had boycotted the Lok Sabha proceedings over the matter, but BJP leader Vijay Kumar Malhotra was also of the opinion that the decision of the House was paramount. But Malhotra suggested that the Speaker need not appear himself, but a public prosecutor could put his case before the court. In this case, the Lok Sabha had decided to disqualify 10 MPs and a Rajya Sabha member. Last month, a TV channel showed 11 MPs allegedly accepting bribes in exchange for asking questions. Following the uproar, special committees were formed in both the houses which recommended the sacking of the MPs. And then after voting on it, it was decided that the membership of the MPs should be terminated. The sacked MPs then approached the Supreme Court and the court issued a notice to the Lok Sabha Speaker. The MPs were of the view that all this was an interference in the domain of Parliament, as the Supreme Court, in a landmark judgment on the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha in the 1990s, had also held that the courts had no role to play in the affairs within Parliament. The Speaker underlined that he was not taking the path of confrontation. But this is the second time in the last few months that MPs have objected to the court's attitude. Even when the courts objected to the proposal for reservation in private educational institutions, Parliament saw fit to pass the new law. It is now up to the public to see if Parliament and the judiciary are heading for a confrontation.

The Maoists have announced a boycott of these elections. This has led to an increased risk of violence and panic among candidates. The withdrawal of candidates meant that there would be no candidates for nearly a thousand of the 4,146 seats up for election on February 8. The administration has kept hundreds of candidates in safe houses to protect them from Maoist attacks. Seventy candidates in the Janakpurdham area have been kept under tight security at a government training centre. Reports are coming in from all over the country that the candidates are being forced to withdraw their names by their distressed wives and scared relatives. There are also reports that the authorities pressured some people to stand for election. There are no candidates in 60 per cent of the seats reserved for women. Many districts have only one candidate and no one to challenge them. Election Commission spokesman Tejmuni Bajracharya said, "Only 36 municipalities will go to the polls as there are no candidates in the remaining 22 municipalities." The government of Nepal's King Gyanendra says the elections will pave the way for further growth of democracy. The opposition boycotts, but in addition to the Maoists, the major opposition parties have also decided to boycott these elections. The opposition says the king is holding the elections to justify his hold on power. Maharaja Gyanendra took direct control of the power in February 2005. In Kathmandu, a rebel leader has issued a direct warning to those taking part in the elections that the consequences would be very bad if they did so. Maharaja Gyanendra has promised to hold general elections in Nepal by mid-2007.

Representatives of medical colleges across the country on Monday decided to continue the strike after considering the Supreme Court order. Notably, medical students are on strike to protest against the reservation for students from backward castes in higher education institutions run with the support of the central government. Despite the strike, the government has announced that the reservation will come into effect from June 2007. However, the government has promised to take into account the interests of all sections and preparations are being made to increase seats in the institutions for this. The students have welcomed the Supreme Court's order issuing a notice to the central government asking what is the basis for giving reservation to backward classes. Medical students have said they are not calling off the strike but will run parallel OPDs outside the hospital. Meanwhile, the strike, which started from Delhi, has spread to several cities and is getting support from people from other walks of life besides medical students. Medical students are holding a rally in Delhi on Monday while in Ahmedabad, strikes have been called in private hospitals besides government hospitals.

Meanwhile, Afghan President Hamid Karzai has made a major reshuffle in the police department, firing several top officials. Security personnel retaliated after suspected Taliban militants attacked a police post in the town of Miyana Shein on Saturday, Kandahar governor's spokesman Dawood Ahmadi said, briefing about the encounter. He said 12 suspected Taliban attackers were killed and four policemen were also wounded in the encounter. In another similar incident, 18 suspected Taliban militants have been arrested in Helmand province adjacent to Kandahar. Taliban militants have stepped up attacks in southern parts of Afghanistan in recent days. Administrative reshuffle About 80 senior police officers have been dismissed or transferred under the reshuffle in the administrative department. The move follows violent protests against the US military in the capital Kabul in recent days. On the other hand, according to the President's Office, this is a part of the plan to reform the police service. An Afghan Interior Ministry official acknowledged that the process was expedited after what happened in Kabul last Monday. Last month, human rights group Human Right Watch told Karzai that many of the police officers who are in talks to be promoted are guilty of human rights violations.

A decision on who will win the 2006 World Cup trophy will be made on Sunday evening. The final is between 1998 World Cup winners France and three-time World Cup winners Italy. This is the first time since 1982 that the final is being played between two European countries. In 1982, Italy defeated then-West Germany 3-1. The victory in the 1998 final remains France's best performance at the World Cup to date. While the Italian team has won the title in 1934, 1938 and 1982. France and Italy have played 32 matches against each other so far, of which 17 have been against Italy, seven against France and the remaining eight have ended in draws. The Euro 2000 final was also contested between France and Italy. The match was won 1-2 by France with the golden goal. There have been no matches between the two countries since. As far as the players are concerned, all eyes will be on France's Zinedine Zidane and Thierry Onri. Zinedine Zidane and Liliang Thuriam will play their last matches for France. Both have announced their retirement after the World Cup. While the Italian captain will be playing in his 100th match. Italy have scored a total of 11 goals in the Football World Cup 2006 and if the Italian team wins the final this time, it will become the second team to win the World Cup at least four times. So far, only Brazil has managed to win the football World Cup five times. For the first time since 1978, there will be no Germany or Brazil in the final.

The two presidents discussed bilateral and other international issues ahead of the G-8 meeting in St. Petersburg. Russian and US officials have said that even at this meeting of the two leaders, no bilateral understanding could be reached that would pave the way for Russia to become a member of the World Trade Organization (WTO). President Bush has said that this needs to be discussed further because he wants to be sure that any such understanding, if any, is approved in the US Congress. Negotiators from both countries held intensive talks on the issue for several days, and the two leaders had a late-night conversation before the G8 meeting, trying hard to reach an agreement. The BBC's economic affairs correspondent says the failure of the talks is a major blow to Russian President Vladimir Putin, who had hoped for a positive outcome ahead of the G8 meeting. According to critics, the talks would have raised issues of energy security, the Middle East, besides Russia's accession to the World Trade Organization (WTO). President Bush reiterated Friday that he stands by the concerns he has been raising about internal freedoms in Russia. Russian President Putin has been critical of the United States for repeatedly raking up the issue. Energy security Putin has responded sharply to Western critics in recent days, advising them to abandon their "colonialist" attitude and refrain from interfering in Russia's internal affairs. The G-8, a group of wealthy countries, believes Russia can play a key role in maintaining a safe supply of energy sources they need. Russia, on the other hand, wants to guarantee the safety of its customers.

In Holland, in 1928, his stick was broken and checked to see if it contained any magnets. In 1932, Japanese players said that glue was stuck to Dhyan Chand's stick, and in 1936, Hitler invited the player from the team that defeated the German team 8 − 1 at the UK Olympics to a high position in his army. A few years ago, Dhyan Chand's wife, the late Janaki Dhyan Chand, said, "It was Hitler's time. They saw people standing around with flags of their respective countries. The Indian team stood as it was. He felt very sad that this was our condition. Then, when he stepped onto the field, he scored consistently. "Simplicity was reflected in Major Dhyan Chand's patriotism and his simplicity in his hockey. Dhyan Chand's son Ashok Kumar, a former Indian captain, remembers his father, saying, "He led a simple life and played with friends who were close to him. He scolded us many times when we lost. He used to say, "If the team won, he gave all the credit to his teammates and if the team lost, he took all the responsibility." Former Olympian Commander Nandy Singh has played with Major Dhyan Chand and recalls, "The world says that the ball used to stick with his hockey. He didn't keep the ball to himself. It is a misconception that he used to dribble the ball. He didn't dribble at all. His speciality was the goal score. He could score goals from any angle. "Major Dhyan Chand was the coach and selector of the legendary centre-forward Harbinder Singh, who played in the Indian team from the Tokyo Olympics to the Munich Olympics. Harbinder Singh recalls, "There was a camp in Patiala. Dada used to get very angry when someone missed a goal. The amount of hockey I played and the education that Dada Dhyan Chand gave me was very rewarding. "Popularity After independence and partition in 1952, Dhyan Chand was travelling through Pakistan to Afghanistan. During this time, former international hockey referee KG Kakkar became an eyewitness to Dhyan Chand's popularity. "When we reached Lahore, it was so crowded that the platform tickets were exhausted. Everyone wanted to meet Dhyan Chand and when the train reached Peshawar, it was three hours late. "And the hockey wizard, who had gathered a crowd of his fans from Delhi to Peshawar, ended his last journey at the ground in his hometown of Jhansi where he had learned to play his stick.

A geyser is a type of hot spring that bursts from time to time, releasing hot water and steam. Geysers require favourable hydrography, which exists only in a few places on Earth. How are these geysers made... The water on the Earth's surface seeps into the ground and hits a rock that is warming with magma. This causes the water to heat up and then rise and burst out through a rock crack. There are about a thousand geysers in the world, half of which are in Yellowstone National Park in the United States. The name of the electrical machine (geyser) used to use hot water may also be derived from this. Jitendra Kumar Paswan from village Pahlam, Saharsa Bihar, asks which country was the first to host the Olympic Games. The ancient Olympic Games were first played in the Greek city of Olympia, but the history of the modern Olympic Games dates back to 1896 when the games were once again played in Greece. Since then, the Games have been held every four consecutive years. Except for 1940 and 1944 when the Games could not take place due to World War I. Ramchandra Mahato from Khetko, Hazaribagh Jharkhand wants to know which is the most expensive book in the world and who is its author. English author Geoffrey Chaucer's Canterbury Tales can be considered the most expensive book ever written. At an auction in 1998, a copy of the first edition sold for £4.6 million and was purchased by Mags Brothers, a London-based bookseller. This first edition was printed in 1477 and only a dozen copies were printed. What kind of institution is the National School of Drama? Ask Parvez Alam Khan from village Pathrahi, Madhubani Bihar. The National School of Drama is the most important theatre training institute in Delhi. It was established by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 1959. The school has a three-year curriculum with the first year covering all theatre-related subjects, including Eastern and Western theatre literature, acting, silent acting, yoga, music, theatre-technology, stage-decor, costume design, and makeup. In the second year, you specialize in either acting or design and direction. After three years, you get a diploma. To get into the National School of Drama, you must have a BA or its equivalent degree and have some theatre experience. The entrance test is conducted in different parts of the country and the selected candidates are called to Delhi for a workshop. Those who succeed in it get admission. A diploma from the National School of Drama is considered equivalent to a master's degree. What is the full name of HIV, the virus that causes AIDS, and who discovered it and when? Which country has the highest number of people infected with HIV? Village Nainaghat, Darbhanga Bihar to Kallu. The full name of HIV is Human Immunodeficiency Virus. The virus weakens the human body's immune system, leading to AIDS or Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome. It is believed that in 1984, Dr. Robert Gallo of the National Cancer Institute in the United States, Dr. Luc Montagnier of the Pasteur Institute in Paris, and Dr. Jay Levy of the University of California discovered the retrovirus that causes AIDS. The three research groups had named it separately, but then the name HIV was agreed upon. South Africa has the highest number of people infected with HIV. According to the data, about 53 lakh people are affected by this virus and India is in the second place where about 51 lakh people are affected by it. Sunil Gupta via BBC Hindi.com has asked where Mangal Pandey originally hailed from. Mangal Pandey hailed from Nagwa village in Ballia district of Uttar Pradesh. He was a 5th Company sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry Regiment of the East India Company. The Indian soldiers were protesting the use of a new type of cartridge that was allegedly loaded with cow and pig fat and had to be cut through the mouth. There were other reasons for the discontent against Company Raj. On 29 March 1857, Mangal Pandey attacked a British officer at Barrackpore, near Calcutta, after which he was court-martialed and hanged. After this incident, the fire of discontent against the British spread to such an extent that it took the form of Ghadar.

Israeli police had been investigating the case for several weeks. Attorney General Menachem Mazzuz has been briefed by Israeli police on his opinion. The attorney general now has the final say on whether President Katsav will stand trial. President Katsav denies the allegation that he forced two female employees to have sex with him. They also deny allegations of phone tapping and fraud. President Katsav could have to resign if Attorney General Menachem Mazzuz decides that the trial should go ahead. Katsav, 61, is a member of the right-wing Likud party and has held the post since 2000. He is a father of five children and has refused to resign. Although Moshe Katsav is due to start a new session of parliament on Monday, several lawmakers have threatened to walk out if he comes to parliament. India has also expressed concern over the current situation in Sri Lanka. The meeting with Indian leaders and President Rajapaksa is expected to discuss the situation in the territory controlled by the LTTE as well as the peace deal. However, President Rajapaksa's talks with Indian leaders do not appear to be possible before Tuesday. Because President Rajapaksa is going to Dehradun first. He will meet Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on Wednesday. This is Mahinda Rajapaksa's second visit to India after assuming the office of the President a year ago. On Friday, Indian Foreign Secretary Shivshankar Menon returned from a visit to Sri Lanka. India's concern Foreign Secretary Shivshankar Menon had gone to Colombo to convey India's concern to Sri Lanka. India is particularly concerned about the situation on the Jaffna peninsula, where food is not reaching half a million people. Recently, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh assured Tamil Nadu Chief Minister K Karunanidhi that he would convey India's concerns to President Mahinda Rajapaksa. About 60 million people in Tamil Nadu are deeply connected to Sri Lanka's Tamil minority on cultural and religious grounds. As of October 2006, 403 SEZs in the country have either been formally approved or have received in-principle approval. If we talk about principles, the purpose of SEZs is basically: to promote exports. The way property developers have jumped on the SEZ, it looks like whether exports will go up or not, property rates will go up very fast. The Reserve Bank of India has also expressed concern in this regard. The interest of property developers can be gauged from the fact that 46 SEZs have been sanctioned in Haryana, a state favoured by property companies. Inequality Ten per cent of the total sanctioned SEZs have been sanctioned in a state with no far-flung ports. Ports are closely linked to the SEZs, with most of the cargo movement taking place by sea and not by air. Therefore, the SEZ cases in the coastal states will prove to be more fortunate. It is no coincidence that only two coastal southern states account for about 25 per cent of the total sanctioned SEZs. 54 in Andhra Pradesh and 46 in Karnataka. In addition to these, 75 proposals for Maharashtra and 30 for Gujarat form the हैं.पूरी picture, with the four states of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Gujarat accounting for over 50% of the total approved SEZs. Uttar Pradesh has only 18 SEZs, Madhya Pradesh has only 10, Rajasthan has only 11. Bihar needs development the most, but not a single SEZ is proposed there. Karnataka will emerge as the most important state in this entire scenario. Right now, about three per cent of the national GDP comes from Bangalore, just one city in Karnataka, thanks to software exporters including Infosys. New investments will come here due to the new SEZ. North India has traditionally lagged far behind in the map of industrial development. In such a situation, lagging behind in terms of SEZs will push North India further back. According to a study by the National Productivity Council, Bihar was ranked seventh among fifteen states in terms of law and order, followed by Uttar Pradesh at ninth. Karnataka was number one, Bangalore's position makes it clear. In fact, the perspective of regional development should also be taken into account in the development of SEZs. North Indian states do not have ports, they cannot do anything about it, but software exports do not require a port. Its trading is possible only through computers and internet lines. It is better, therefore, for software firms to be oriented towards North India and manufacturing units to go south or to Gujarat or Maharashtra. Why can't Bihar and Uttar Pradesh become important SEZ centres for software? Can the Indian economy be considered developed without these large states being developed in terms of population? These are important questions related to regional development. But sadly, no one has the time to answer these questions, neither policymakers, nor leaders, nor property barons.

Researchers from Germany and Switzerland, in a study of 1676 patients, found that the number of obese patients dying three years after treatment was half that of normal-weight people. However, the study, published in the European Heart Journal, did not provide a reason why obese patients were less likely to die. Experts also reported that obese people are also more likely to develop heart disease. The study involved 1676 hospitalized patients with unstable angina and heart failure. "There is no doubt that obese people are more likely to develop diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease," said lead researcher Dr Heinz Butner. Our study showed that obese people are more likely to be healthy than normal-weight people once the heart artery is treated properly. "The reasons are that obese people look younger than normal-weight people and can be discharged from the hospital with certain heart disease medications. But Dr. Butner said his research doesn't exactly show the cause of the low mortality rate. This, he said, could be due to changes in the body caused by obesity. Obese people tend to have higher amounts of fat that produce protective effects. Also, blood platelet levels are higher in obese patients who play an effective role in blood clotting. "This research raises more questions than it answers," says June Davison of the British Heart Foundation, which studies cardiovascular diseases in the UK. More research needs to be done in this area.
