Supporters of the Samajwadi Party and the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena clashed in Mumbai on the 3rd of this month following Raj Thackeray's controversial statement against North Indians. There were allegations that workers of the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena had beaten up Samajwadi Party supporters. Raj Thackeray's statement was sharply criticised by several other leaders, including Lalu Prasad Yadav and Amar Singh. The dispute had turned violent. Raj Thackeray's supporters had beaten up North Indian taxi drivers and vandalised their taxis. In protest, the Mumbai Taxi Union went on strike for a few hours on the 7th. However, the strike was later withdrawn following an assurance from the deputy chief minister. Following the incident, the Maharashtra government was under pressure to arrest Raj Thackeray. Last week, Mumbai Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh had said, "We are consulting the Advocate General regarding the arrest warrant. The police will act on his advice. "Last Saturday, Raj Thackeray once again targeted North Indians in a special article published in the Marathi daily'Maharashtra Times '. "Even if the whole world opposes me on this issue, my party and I will continue to fight for Marathi culture, Marathis and give a befitting reply to the hooliganism of the people of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar," he said. He had said that despite being a resident of Maharashtra, Amitabh did not do anything special for the state. Earlier, Raj Thackeray had said that people from Bihar are demonstrating their political power in Mumbai by doing the'drama of Chhath '.

Richard Thomas, the UK's information commissioner, said the issue was "serious and controversial" and that the documents should be made public. This is a major setback for the UK government as it has been reluctant to make this information public. Before the Iraq war, there were two important meetings of the British Cabinet. Now people may know what happened at these meetings and this has been made possible by the unprecedented decision of the UK Information Commissioner. However, the UK government had stated that this information should not be made public and had given two reasons for this. First, it will affect the overall responsibility of the cabinet, and second, leaders will shy away from talking about an issue openly in important meetings. The argument was insufficient, but Information Commissioner Richard Thomas found these reasons insufficient, saying the public had a right to know the real cause of the Iraq war. It's an important decision. The public may now know which British minister questioned the Iraq war, who opposed the war, and in what detail the entire issue was debated by the cabinet. The Liberal Democrats, Britain's third-largest party, have welcomed the announcement to make the information public. "The wall of secrecy that the Labour Party built to work in secret is breaking down brick by brick," says Ed Dewey, the party's foreign affairs spokesman. The Labour Party has hidden a lot, and thanks to the Information Commissioner, the public will know the truth in some time, but it is a shame that the government is being stripped of documents one by one. "Downing Street officials say they are considering appealing. At the same time, he has also said that even after the document is made public, not much information may come out because the minutes of cabinet meetings are not taken in much detail, not every word is written.

Besides Mehsud, four others have also been booked in the case, Chaudhry Abdul Majeed, the chief officer investigating the case, said. After registering the case in the court, the judge has also issued a non-bailable warrant for the arrest of the five suspected accused. On 27 December, former Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto was killed in a suicide attack in Rawalpindi. Influence Baitullah Mehsud lives in the South Waziristan region bordering Afghanistan. The area is under the influence of pro-Taliban militants. However, Mehsud has already denied his role in the case. There are also allegations that Baitullah Mehsud is linked to the extremist organisation Al-Qaeda. The Pakistani government has already questioned Baitullah Mehsud's role in the assassination of Benazir Bhutto. President Pervez Musharraf has also named Mehsud in the Benazir assassination case. Baitullah Mehsud is the commander of the Tehreek-e-Taliban. The militant group is believed to have links to Al-Qaeda. Speaking to reporters, Chief Investigating Officer Abdul Majeed refused to elaborate on the investigation into the murder nor did he give any details about the role of the suspected accused. Apart from Baitullah Mehsud, the four accused are Ibadur Rahman, Imramullah, Faiz Mohammad and Abdullah, they said.

The autobiography was released on Wednesday by the country's former President APJ Abdul Kalam in Delhi. The timing of the ceremony was no less than any award function. Be it Anil Ambani from the industry, Sanjay Dutt and Sonu Nigam from the film world or media giants like Cho Ramaswamy. There was no dearth of big people at the event. Almost all senior leaders of the BJP were also present at the launch. Be it Jaswant Singh, Bhairav Singh Shekhawat and Murli Manohar Joshi of the senior generation or Narendra Modi and Rajnath Singh of the new generation. Everyone found time for this release. NDA convenor George Fernandes, RSS's Mohan Bhagwat and NCP's Sharad Pawar also attended the ceremony. In this important book, LK Advani has mentioned many turning points and important events in the politics of the last 60 years of India. These include Partition of India, Emergency and BJP's Rath Yatra. Advani has also written on several sensitive issues such as the Babri Masjid and the 2002 Gujarat riots in this book. At the event, Jaswant Singh stressed that Advani was misunderstood in many ways. "In today's politics, I think Advani ji has been misunderstood and projected. From his personal experience, I can say that he is very different from this image of himself in reality. "On this occasion, Advani described his personal family and his ideological family, the RSS, as a source of meaning and satisfaction in his life. Former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee was not present at the event but Advani expressed his gratitude to him as well. And then finally, the chief guest of the event, A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, described Advani as a creative leader and said of the book, "I agree with what Atal Bihari Vajpayee wrote in the introduction to this book that the best time in the life of a sensitive man and a great leader is yet to come." There are very few leaders in India who have written their autobiography while in active politics. Advani has become one of them. But there has been speculation that the timing of the book's release has been timed to reflect the country's political climate when the clouds of next year's general elections are already setting in. Whatever the reason, in the context of the role that LK Advani has played in the country's politics, this book can perhaps shed new light on many historical events in the country.

Yousuf Raza Gilani said in parliament on Monday that the judges who were detained during the emergency on the orders of President Pervez Musharraf would order their release. The wire outside Judge Chaudhry's house was removed on Monday after the announcement of the new prime minister, Geelani. When Iftikhar Chowdhury, who was in a happy mood, came to the balcony of his house, he was welcomed by hundreds of supporters standing outside the house. "I thank the entire country that has struggled for the last five months," he said in a loudspeaker address. "" I have no words to express how grateful I am to you people. "" In November, Pervez Musharraf ordered the detention of several judges. " He dismissed several judges, including Iftikhar Chaudhry, under the Emergency. As soon as the Emergency was imposed, President General Pervez Musharraf handed over the responsibility of the post of Chief Justice to Justice Abdul Hamid Dogar. State media have quoted a senior administration official as saying that all dismissed judges are free to move about. Earlier on Monday, parliament elected Yousuf Raza Gilani as the country's new prime minister. He received a total of 242 votes.

The BSP has also won the parliamentary seats of Azamgarh and Khalilabad, as well as the assembly seats of Bilgram, Karnailganj and Murad Nagar. The Congress and the Bharatiya Janata Party have suffered a major setback in this by-election. To a certain extent, the BSP's fight was with the Samajwadi Party. Kushal Tiwari of BSP won the Khalilabad parliamentary seat defeating Balchandra Yadav of Samajwadi Party by a margin of sixty-five thousand votes. BSP's Akbar Ahmad Dumpy won the Azamgarh parliamentary seat. He defeated Samajwadi Party's Ramakant Yadav, who contested on a Bharatiya Janata Party ticket, by a margin of 54,000 votes. The Congress candidate received less than ten thousand votes in this seat. Both these seats were won by BSP's Balchandra Yadav and Ramakant Yadav in the last Lok Sabha elections, but both the parties switched to the Samajwadi Party. The two seats fell vacant under the defection law. Rajni Yadav of BSP won the Bilgram assembly seat. The seat had fallen vacant after the death of BSP's Upendra Tiwari. While Kunwari Brij Singh of BSP won the Karnalganj assembly seat, Rajpal Tyagi won the Murad Nagar assembly seat. Rajpal Tyagi won the state assembly election from here as an independent candidate but he later joined the BSP. He managed to win the seat again by defeating Ayub Khan of the Lok Dal. Uttar Pradesh has completed 11 months of Mayawati's rule. These by-election results have further strengthened his position.

The festival, which began on Friday evening, screened the film Insaaf Ka Scale. Classic films like Chhoti Si Baat, Naya Daur, and Saam will be seen during the festival. BR Chopra himself did not attend the ceremony due to ill health. सके.फ़िल्मोत्सव was inaugurated by BR Chopra's brother and noted filmmaker Yash Chopra. He said, "My brother made his own films - that too at a time when people were apprehensive about the commercial success of such films because these films were different, the kind of stories that were in vogue at that time, the stories of BR Chopra ji were different from them." BR Chopra raised many topics like widow remarriage, prostitution in his films. Memorable films His film Naya Daur in 1957 reflects the ideals of the Nehru era while Sadhana in 1958 questions the society on the issue of prostitution. Films such as Gumrah, Hamraaz, Kanoon and Nikah feature on the list of films he has produced. Although most of BR Chopra's films were based on some social issue or the other, these experimental films also did well at the box office. The story of Naya Daur was turned down by many top directors but BR Chopra took the risk and made the film. Speaking on the occasion, Ravi Chopra, son of BR Chopra, said, "My father believes in getting the job done. For me, he is and will remain the best director. "The colour version of Naya Daur was also released some time ago. A short documentary on the life of BR Chopra was also screened at the film festival. Apart from Yash Chopra, the event was attended by Raj Babbar, director Basu Chatterjee, music composer Ravi and producer Bobby Bedi.

The ceasefire along the Line of Control separating the disputed territory of Jammu and Kashmir has been in place since November 2003. Colonel AK Mathur, an Indian Army spokesman, said on Wednesday that Pakistani troops opened fire in the Tangdhar sector near the LoC on Tuesday evening. This is the first reported incident of shelling along the Line of Control after the ceasefire. No one was reported injured in this shelling. "Our forces did not retaliate," a military spokesman said. We have formally requested a'flag meeting'to register our protest and resolve the issue. "Notably, the alleged ceasefire violation comes at a time when Pakistan has a democratically elected government. The new government of Pakistan has been talking about furthering bilateral relations with India. India says Pakistan has so far not been successful in eliminating militant training camps in its territory along the LoC.

Wali Karzai, the president of the provincial assembly of Kandahar and the brother of President Hamid Karzai, told the BBC that there were 1,000 prisoners in the prison at the time and that all had escaped. It is believed that 350 of these prisoners were Taliban. Several security personnel have lost their lives in the attack. According to officials, a lorry bomb was detonated to blow up the main gate of the prison and then 40 Taliban entered the prison. A state of emergency has been declared in the city of Kandahar. Police and soldiers are patrolling the streets and people have been told not to leave their homes. Prison chief Abdul Qabir confirmed to the AP that hundreds of prisoners had escaped, but said some stayed behind bars. Eyewitnesses say the blast, which was aimed at breaking the main gate of the jail, was so powerful that window panes were shattered up to three kilometres away. The BBC's Kabul correspondent on the protests says it is an incident that will worry the Afghan police and other security forces. Kandahar is one of the select locations from where the war is being fought against the Taliban, who are rebelling against President Karzai, NATO and US forces. Just last month, prisoners in Kandahar jail went on a hunger strike and the strike ended on the assurance of a parliamentary party that their demands would be met. Some 400 prisoners said they were not getting proper justice, many of whom also complained of torture.

Brigadier Uday Nanyakara, a military spokesman, blamed the attack on Tamil rebels. The incident took place in Monargala district when indiscriminate firing took place on this bus. There has been no comment from the LTTE on the incident so far. The attack comes as clashes between the army and Tamil rebels have intensified in the northern part of the country. A BBC reporter from Colombo has reported that the bus was passing through a noisy area when shots were fired at it. A nine-year-old child is among those killed in the attack. Several passengers were also injured in the firing. Military spokesman Brigadier Uday Nanyakara says the gunmen were probably hiding on the side of the road. He has blamed Tamil rebels for the shooting. A year ago, the Sri Lankan government claimed to have driven the rebels from the eastern part, but sporadic violence continued in the region. In January of the same year, rebels also targeted a passenger bus. The bus was first attacked with a bomb and then people were shot. Just last week, a helicopter was also shot down. Meanwhile, fighting between the LTTE and government forces continues in northern Sri Lanka. The military says 19 Tamil rebels and two soldiers were killed on Thursday.

A special session of Parliament has begun where a confidence motion will be moved shortly. The debate will be followed by a vote of confidence on Tuesday to see how the manipulation of various parties over the past fifteen days plays out. Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee has called an all-party meeting ahead of the confidence motion in the House and all parties are participating in it. Prime Minister Manmohan Singh is expected to move a one-line motion for a vote of confidence in the Lok Sabha on Monday that "this House expresses its confidence in the Council of Ministers." The motion will then be discussed in the Lok Sabha on Monday and Tuesday and the Prime Minister will once again respond to the discussion followed by a division of votes that will decide the fate of the government. A time limit of 16 hours has been fixed for the debate but given the current circumstances, the debate may go beyond that. Apart from the Prime Minister, the names of Sonia Gandhi, Pranab Mukherjee, Sitaram Yechury, LK Advani and many other big leaders are being taken in the debate. The hard test is that the vote of one MP out of 543 MPs in Parliament is not valid, which would mean a majority among 542 MPs. That is, 271 votes are needed for a majority and it is not yet fully clear which alliance has how many MPs. The situation is such that big leaders are even reluctant to answer questions about how many MPs are with them. While the Congress-led alliance has the support of Shibu Soren's JMM, there are reports that some Congress MPs may vote against the party. The same is the case with the Samajwadi Party, where at least five MPs are set to vote against the UPA, contrary to the party's stance. The Bharatiya Janata Party may be the main opposition party in the opposition coalition parliament but in the manipulations and developments of the last one week, Mayawati has left the BJP far behind. Mayawati has been successful in getting Ajit Singh's Rashtriya Lok Dal on her side and JD (S )'s SD Deve Gowda has also joined her. Together with the Left, Mayawati has succeeded in creating an alternative. However, the picture is still unclear as according to latest reports, some MPs from the Akali Dal and Shiv Sena may also go and vote against their party whips. Amid this state of speculation and confusion, the debate on the confidence motion is going to start soon.

The IAEA's approval was necessary towards implementing the nuclear deal. Following the IAEA's approval, India will now have to seek the consent of the 45-member Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG). So that India can get involved in the nuclear fuel trade. The Indo-US nuclear deal will then need the approval of the US Congress. India remains under pressure to get the agreement passed and ratified by the US Congress before the US presidential election in November. Nuclear deal Recently, the Indian government had to move a vote of confidence in Parliament over the same nuclear deal. This was because the Left parties, which were supporting the government from outside, had withdrawn support to the government on the issue of the nuclear deal. But the government won the trust vote. India argues that the nuclear deal is necessary for the country's growing energy needs. During the meeting, IAEA chief Mohammed Al Baradei said the safety standards of India's nuclear power institutions are in line with the agency's. "This is meeting India's needs as well as the IAEA's statutory requirements," he said. "After this agreement, IAEA observers will monitor Indian civilian nuclear sites so that nuclear fuel is not used for military purposes." Under the agreement with the US, India will be able to make its presence felt in the international market for nuclear fuel and technology. But it has to be used for civilian or civilian purposes only. BBC reporters say that now after the agreement with the IAEA, 14 of India's existing 22 nuclear sites will come under the IAEA's surveillance.

Three helicopters of the Indian Air Force are also engaged in the distribution of relief material. Additional Commissioner of the Disaster Management Department Pratyay Amit told news agency PTI that the Kosi embankment near a village in Nepal has also broken, which is now bringing more water and has flooded many other areas. Around 100 army personnel will be engaged in relief operations in Madhepura from Wednesday, he said. Apart from this, personnel of Sashastra Seema Bal, Special Forces and National Disaster Response Force are also helping. The flood-ravaged districts of Araria, Supaul and Madhepura adjoining Nepal have been the worst affected by the breach of the embankment of the Kosi. According to government officials, 20 to 25 lakh people have been rendered homeless. According to the information received so far, 40 people have died, but the exact loss of life and property will be assessed only after the flood surge subsides. Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar described the situation as "alarming." Officials have said that the situation is bad and massive rescue and relief operations have been carried out. 200 pistols and 25 motor boats are being pressed into service for rescue operations. Helicopters have been pressed into service to transport food packets to the affected areas. More than 50 camps have been set up, officials said. People have taken shelter in highways and high-rise buildings to avoid flooding. "Nearby 700-800 houses have been damaged," Sanjeev Kumar, a flood victim, told Reuters news agency. People are somehow stuck on the logs and roofs of houses. The houses whose roofs have been damaged do not know what to do. "On Tuesday morning, 100 prisoners from two jails in Bihar were taken to other safer jails. According to reports, the floods have damaged standing crops on thousands of hectares of land. The Bihar government has appealed to relief agencies to help bring relief to the flood-affected areas. However, many say they have not received any help so far. "No arrangements have been made," flood-affected Jugat Lal told Reuters. We live near the river, and drink its water when thirsty, although it also causes deaths. "Meanwhile, heavy rains and floods have killed 700 people since June in the neighbouring state of Uttar Pradesh. According to officials, most of the deaths were caused by house collapses.

Some of these films are releasing and some are in production. Nishikant Kamath's film Mumbai Meri Jaan, released last week, was based on the Mumbai train bombings of 11 July 2006. About 200 people were killed in the bombings. Nishikant Kamath, the director of the film says, "The film depicts an attempt to recover from a major accident. The story of Mumbai Meri Jaan is not just about Mumbai or this incident but about how people are dealing with this problem. "Mumbai Meri Jaan is an emotional film while'Wednesday ', which is going to be released on 5th September, is a thriller. Director Neeraj Pandey, who made his directorial debut with the film, says, "Wednesday is about a few hours in which terrorists try to make the city of Mumbai a victim of their terror. The film is set against the backdrop of terrorism and is entirely shot in Mumbai, but the story of the film is entirely fictional. "The recently released psycho-thriller'Aamir'was the story of a common man who is blackmailed and forced to place bombs in some areas of Mumbai. The film did well and was appreciated by critics as well. The film'The Little Godfather ', being made under the banner Popcorn Films, is also based on the Mumbai bombings. Contemporary The Little Godfather is the story of small children who sell goods on Mumbai's local trains and how those children displayed bravery on the day of the bombing. The film's director, Joy Augustine, believes that people quickly associate themselves with real events. He says, "The story of the film is about the common people who travel in Mumbai trains and the children who sell goods in these trains and how these people bond with each other during such calamities." Even film critics see this as a big change. But he says it's temporary. Senior film critic Ajay Brahmatmaj says, "Films may have bombs in the background, but producers and directors don't want to make a film entirely on it, and perhaps that's because they don't want to get into any controversy." Just like in the old films, some incidents like floods, fairs were used to give a twist to the story, bomb blasts are being used these days, they will change with time. "Such films are generally shorter than three hours, they have less space for music and romance. Directors like Ram Gopal Varma, who has made many successful films on the Mumbai underworld, have also tried to portray the fast-growing relationship between the underworld and terrorism in his recently released film'Contract '. Alpana Mishra of UTV believes that it is a coincidence that somewhere in the stories of UTV's recent releases, bomb blasts or terrorism play an important part. We are happy that these films of ours are also carrying a social message, she says.

The situation in Orissa is tense after the murder of Vishwa Hindu Parishad leader Swami Lakshmanananda. Koraput district was away from violent activities but tensions erupted on Saturday over objectionable content written against a particular community on the walls of the local Vikram Dev College. This led to a clash between the two communities. Police first resorted to lathicharge and lobbed tear gas shells to disperse the mob involved in the clash. Failing to control the mob, the police opened fire in the air. Curfew Koraput Superintendent of Police Deepak Kumar said that curfew has been imposed in the city. He himself was injured in the clash. The violent mob also attacked the police station and damaged furniture. The problem began when angry youths started attacking students from other communities over what was written on the walls. At least two girls were injured in the incident. The VHP alleges that Christian organisations are behind the killing of their leader in Kandhamal. However, there has been no official word from the government so far. It is also suspected that Maoist rebels may be behind the killing.

This phase of polling is scheduled to be held on November 20. The first phase of polling has been completed on November 14. The counting of votes will take place on December 8. In the second phase too, the state is set to witness several key contests, including the election of former chief minister Ajit Jogi and his wife Renu Jogi. In the same phase, the political future of state Congress president Dhanendra Sahu and working president Satyanarayan Sharma, state BJP president Vishnu Deo Sai and Dilip Singh Judev's son Yudhvir Singh is also to be decided. On the last day of campaigning, several senior leaders from both the major parties, including Sonia Gandhi and LK Advani, were on the campaign trail. In the first phase, elections were also held in Bastar in south Chhattisgarh, an area affected by the Naxalite movement. There were several reports of violence during polling in 12 tribal seats of Bastar. Tribal seats in northern Chhattisgarh are up for election this time, and many areas associated with Jharkhand are also counted among the areas affected by the Naxalite or Maoist movement. However, the Maoist influence here is not the same as in areas of Bastar. A total of 15 tribal seats are up for election in this phase, while six seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and 30 seats are general. The political fate of 687 candidates is to be decided in these 51 seats. These include Home Minister Ramvichar Netam, Health Minister Amar Agarwal, former Home Minister Nandkumar Patel and NCP state president Nobel Verma. Of these 51 seats, the Congress has left three seats for its political ally NCP, while the BJP and the BSP have fielded candidates in all 51 seats. Since Chief Minister Raman Singh's election was over in the first phase, he campaigned vigorously for the second phase while many leaders including BJP president Rajnath Singh, MP Shatrughan Sinha, Hema Malini addressed election meetings. From the Congress side, besides Rahul Gandhi, Vidya Charan Shukla, Motilal Vora, Haryana Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda addressed election rallies. In these elections, while the BJP has raised issues like giving rice to the poor at Rs 3 per kg besides development, the Congress has thrown up corruption in development works and promised to give rice at Rs 2 per kg if the government is formed.

The BJP won the last election on the issue of power, water and roads but the party has not achieved any success other than changing three chief ministers in a five-year term. Chief Minister Shivraj Singh is saying that power generation has increased to 6,200 MW under his rule, but he forgets to mention that more than a thousand MW of this power belongs to the central government. What can be a bigger tragedy than this that the electricity produced in Madhya Pradesh does not reach the farmers here but goes to other states. You can guess from this that while the national growth rate is around nine per cent, it is only 3.5 per cent in Madhya Pradesh. When Digvijaya Singh's government was in power, the state was ranked 12th in terms of development, now it is at 14th position. In terms of agriculture, it was at the ninth position, now at the 12th position. It was ranked eighth in terms of industrial growth and is now ranked 15th. "Law and order and corruption" will be a major issue in this election, with deteriorating law and order and corruption in most of the states. The minority community in the state is scared of the BJP's communal politics and feels insecure. Our slogan is that when we come to power, we will give an accountable and honest government to the people. In the case of corruption, the Shivraj government has broken all the old records. Perhaps for the first time in democratic history, cases of corruption have been registered against the 12-13 ministers of a state. Even the Chief Minister has a stain on his hands and the public understands this very well. Inflation is an issue, not a threat from the BSP, but it would not be fair to blame the UPA government at the Centre for it. Prices have gone up all over the world and the state government also has a role to play in stopping prices. We have promised to provide food grains at affordable rates in our manifesto. Some people say that this is not an economically prudent decision, but I would like to say that this decision has been taken only after talking to economic experts. I am confident that the Congress party will get a majority and form the government on its own. (Based on a conversation with BBC correspondent Alok Kumar)

Condoleezza Rice will meet Indian Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and other senior ministers. The US Secretary of State's visit to India follows President George W Bush's assurance that the US is fully with India and will provide all possible assistance in the investigation of the Mumbai attacks. Earlier on Sunday, President George W. Bush called Indian Prime Minister Manmohan Singh. In this conversation, President Bush assured Prime Minister Singh that the United States stands with the Indian people. Condoleezza Rice, ahead of her visit to India, has asked Pakistan to fully cooperate with India in its investigation of the attacks. Meanwhile, US Republican Senator and presidential candidate John McCain suddenly reached Delhi on Tuesday to express his sympathy after the Mumbai attacks. He met Prime Minister Manmohan Singh. He said the US stands with India in this regard. He said Pakistan should fully cooperate with India in the investigation of the case. Advising India not to take military action against Pakistan, McCain said relations between the two countries had improved significantly before the attacks. He said that some elements in Pakistan do not want to see this atmosphere improve. Diplomatic analysts believe that both President Bush's assurances and then Condoleezza Rice's visit are indications that the US is concerned about extremist attacks and is sensitive to India-Pakistan relations.

The Calcutta High Court had directed the registration of a criminal case against these men on a petition by Jagmohan Dalmiya. These people have been severely accused of filing false affidavits. A division bench of the Supreme Court headed by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan passed the direction on a petition by Sharad Pawar and others. In their petition, they had said that the Calcutta High Court delivered the verdict without hearing them. Besides Pawar, the other accused in the case are current BCCI president Shashank Manohar, former secretary Niranjan Shah, senior official Ratnakar Shetty, current secretary N Srinivasan and chairman of the junior cricket committee Chirayu Amin. The Calcutta High Court had given this direction on the charge of filing a false affidavit in the case of former Speaker Jagmohan Dalmiya. Dalmiya was suspended from the BCCI in 2006. He was accused of financial irregularities during the World Cup cricket tournament during his tenure. Dalmiya had challenged the board's decision in court. His suspension was later stayed by the court and Jagmohan Dalmiya was again elected as the president of the Cricket Association of Bengal in the elections held this year. A few months ago, Dalmiya had approached the court over a false affidavit. It was then that the Calcutta High Court, in its order dated 12 November, ordered the initiation of a criminal case against six board officials.

Sourav Ganguly, who was in Delhi to play a Ranji match, told reporters that Yuvraj is a great player of one-day cricket. He said, "I am sure he will prove himself in Test cricket as well." Notably, Yuvraj Singh has replaced Sourav Ganguly after his retirement. Yuvraj made a comeback to Tests after eight months with knocks of 14 and 85 in the first Test against England in Chennai. England set a target of 387 runs for India to win. On the final day of the match, India achieved the target for the loss of four wickets thanks to a fine partnership between Sachin and Yuvraj. Sachin Tendulkar scored a brilliant unbeaten century while Yuvraj Singh scored an unbeaten 85. Indian captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni is quite happy with Yuvraj Singh's current form. During the ODI series against England, Dhoni had said that while it was nice to see Sehwag and Sachin batting on the field, Yuvraj's attitude on the wicket was different. Dhoni said that according to him, Yuvraj looks more aggressive than Sachin and Sehwag when he is in rhythm.

According to the FIEO, this is the first time since 1929 that the international market has deteriorated to the point where there is no demand for Indian goods. At least 10 million jobs will be lost by March, federation president Ek Sakthivel told reporters in New Delhi, according to news agency Press Trust of India. Exports registered a robust growth rate of 30.9% in the first six months of last year, but dropped to just 12% after October. For the first time in the last five years, such a reduction in the export rate has been seen. Not only this, it further decreased in the month of November. "I can say that growth will remain negative in December and not improve in the next few months," Sakthivel said. He said the measures taken by the government last week to revive the economy did not have any impact on the export sector. Last year, the export target was $200 billion, but now it is expected to go up to $180 billion. The figures for December are yet to come. Europe and North America are the largest markets for India's goods, but both regions are suffering from a recession.

Wednesday was the second day of the auction. The Indian government did not receive a very good response on the first day. Only five companies participated. The government has been able to collect only Rs 9,200 crore. This was because the base price for licences for the entire country was ₹14,000 crore, which was quite high. This will have an impact on the people or the industry. Because the'bidding price'is quite high. Telecom companies may increase mobile tariffs as prices are already quite low in India.

Many institutions consider this study to be very important, although this research does not explain what causes hangovers to worsen due to smoking. The researchers asked 113 US students to write in a diary for eight weeks about their drinking and smoking habits and hangover symptoms. Smokers were far worse off when they drank frozen drinks, such as six cans of beer in an hour. The findings of the study have been published in the Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs. One of the authors of the paper'Complex Relationships'is Dr. Damaris Rohzenov says, "People who drink an equal amount of alcohol are more likely to hang out the next day than those who smoke." "Smokers have an increased risk of hangover compared to nonsmokers." A spokesperson for Action on Addiction, an anti-addiction organization, has stressed the need for more research. He says the relationship between alcohol and smoking is complex. "We expect some people to reduce their intake of alcohol, smoking, or both after learning that smoking increases the risk of hangovers," the spokesperson said. The study, conducted at Midwestern University in the US, highlights the amount of alcohol, number of cigarettes, and symptoms of hangovers. These include more than usual fatigue, headaches, nausea, and difficulty concentrating. "Because both alcohol and tobacco interact with brain receptors," says Amanda Stanford, research manager at Action on Smoking and Health. No wonder, then, that smoking increases the risk of hangovers.

The supercomputer Tianhe-2 was also voted the world's most powerful computer in June this year. According to the standard test called LINPAC, Tianhe-2 can calculate 33.86 petaflops per second i.e. 3,38,630 trillions per second. Tianhe-2 first became the world's fastest computer system in June this year. The list, which came out in June, has seen only one change. Computer Peace Dent of Switzerland has secured the sixth position in this list. Piz Dent can calculate at a rate of 6.27 petaflops per second. Led by a professor at the University of Mannheim in Germany, the list of the world's 500 fastest computers is compiled twice a year. Second on the list is American supercomputer Titan, but Tianhe-2's score is almost double that of Titan. Titan is a US Department of Energy supercomputer and is housed at Oak Ridge National Laboratory in the state of Tennessee. Computer speed is measured by solving a special kind of unilinear equation to create a standard list of speeds. This test does not assess parameters such as data transfer in addition to computational speed. While these can affect the performance of the computer during practical use. IBM, the maker of five of the top ten computers on the list, told the BBC in an interview that the methodology for compiling the list now needed to be changed and that the company would address the issue at a conference this week in Denver, Colorado. Dr Alessandro Corrioni, head of the computational science department at IBM's Zurich Research Lab, told the BBC: "Listing the top 500 was a useful way for decades to measure the ability of computers to solve a particular problem and the state of development of high-capacity computers, but now we need to adopt a more pragmatic approach that shows the performance of these supercomputers based on their most important function during practical use." He is second on the list. Eric Strohmaier says, "A simple standard like LinePack cannot predict the actual performance of an application in today's complex computer systems." Tianhe-2 means Milky Way-2 in Chinese. It has been developed by China's National University of Defense Technology. It is located in China's southeastern province of Guangdong. It uses a variety of composite processors made by Intel. It also uses a special type of CPU (Central Processing Unit) designed by the university. However, Professor Ellen Woodward of the Department of Computers at the University of Surrey says it is not yet clear whether China's supercomputer is better than the American computer in practical use. Diamonds are made of carbon purified by extreme heat and pressure at a depth of about 150 kilometers from the Earth's surface. Kimberlite Diamonds are found in Kimberlite. Volcanic eruptions bring diamonds to the Earth's surface, usually deposited in another blue rock, Kimberlite. The presence of kimberlite has indicated the presence of diamonds in many parts of the world, including Africa, Siberia, and Australia. Researchers have found evidence of the presence of kimberlite for the first time in Antarctica. The team of researchers found three specimens on the slopes of Mount Meredith in the northern Prince Charles Mountains. Dr. Teal Riley, a survey geologist with the British Antarctic Survey, said, "Research suggests the discovery of Group One Kimberlite is significant because diamonds are much more likely to be found in this type of Kimberlite." "However, only 10 percent of Group One Kimberlite are economically viable, so it's still a big step forward in promoting the latest discoveries related to any diamond mining activity in Antarctica." Even if diamonds are in abundance in this inhospitable area, there are still some significant legal barriers to their extraction. There is a possibility of diamonds in the frozen region of Antarctica. The Protocol on Environmental Protection to the Antarctic Treaty of 1991 explicitly prohibits any mining activity related to mineral resources except for scientific purposes. However, it is due to be reviewed in 2041 and these provisions may be changed at that time. Dr Kevin Hughes, of the Scientific Committee on Antarctic Research, said: "It is not known what the views of the countries involved in the treaty on mining minerals in the Antarctic will be after 2041. By then, he says, there may be technology that makes mining in the Antarctic economically viable. The findings follow a study of 53,467 women between 2009 and 2013. Scientists have found an "above-average" risk of breast cancer in 14,593 of these women. They hope the study will raise awareness among women and help them make lifestyle changes that will help reduce breast cancer cases. The higher-than-average risk means that such cases have a 3.5% chance of developing breast cancer in the next ten years, the study said. Currently, mammograms are recommended for women aged 50 to 70 once every three years to detect cancer at an early stage and increase the likelihood of treatment being effective. "Prevention will not only protect women from cancer, but also from" "overspending" "on treatment, said lead researcher Professor Gareth Evans from the University of Manchester." The scientists assessed the risk of developing breast cancer in a patient by assessing risk factors such as family history, lifestyle, and collecting genetic information from saliva. They also measured breast tissue density through mammograms and visual assessments, which are indications in a patient of breast cancer. Making some lifestyle changes, such as regular exercise, losing weight, and reducing alcohol consumption, can also reduce the risk of breast cancer by up to 30 percent. "" "This shift will put women's fate in their own hands," "said Professor Evans." An independent review regarding the effectiveness of breast cancer screening was published in 2012, in which the concept of'overtreatment'has been much debated. Further treatment occurs when the tumor is found after proper screening, but is not harmful. This can cause women to undergo unnecessary treatment in the form of surgery, hormone therapy, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy, often with significant side effects. "This study may help in this case," said Professor Michael Marmot, from University College London, who said that women who are at higher risk for breast cancer are more likely to develop severe symptoms of the disease and thus have greater treatment relevance. But he said it is important to assess the importance of a one- or two-year interval of screening in cancer development. One of them is Thikni Devi of Chikni village in Nepal. "When they were born, there was an illness, so the housemates threw them near the river," explains Thodini, 60. He was brought up by a family in the neighbourhood. When he recovered, his father brought him home. The mother had given birth to the name Tholani. "There are cultural stereotypes or other social and economic reasons behind the stuck names. But now such names are becoming less common. 'Samadheen will be called Sridevi'Fenney has named his daughter Snehlata. Snehlata explains, "When the marriage took place, my father-in-law asked,'What is the name of Thozhni Devi? ' Since the mother was beautiful, he said, "We will call our Samaddin Sridevi." My mother kept my name very sweet. "On this changing pattern of ending names, sociologist Hetukar Jha says," Earlier names were given in a way that matched both your caste and status. But now you will get a lot of change in the name. There are two reasons for this - firstly, the influence of all the names that are being received through TV, films, newspapers. The other is breaking the bond of the community or the village. The emphasis has been on individuality. "It seemed strange." Phuljhari Devi is from Sipara, adjacent to Patna. He told BBC Hindi, "At this age, if someone says Phuljhari, it feels very strange. Our names were strange, but keep the children's names nice. My boys were named Dhuria and Kanaria in the village but when they came to the city, I changed them to Shivvachan and Santosh. "The yearning to change such a name is also evident in these women and their families. Khushbu, Phooljhari's granddaughter, says, "I told papa, change the name of the grandmother. But Papa said that in the voter card, old age pension, the grandmother's name is Phuljhari. That is why it is difficult to change the name. "Says Prem Kumar Mani, writer and leader, Bihar Dalit thinker and litterateur," The sense of aesthetics is increasing rapidly among those who are marginalized. And this is a big cultural phenomenon. Those people are now paying attention to their clothes, cups of tea, and names. And now there are no such names in the society. Names like Ghisu, Nanhu, Bhimal are not found even in contemporary literature. "However, Hetukar Jha denies any major change in the name. "It's a change but not just a superficial, profound change that has brought about a change in life or improved its standard of living," he says. The name is just your identity, nothing else. "Changing the name may not have changed people's lives, but people now seem aware of the name. For example, Rajdhani Devi of Sitabigaha in Sasaram says, "It was discovered in the house that the capital is a very big place, so the parents named it Rajdhani. Now when the name is put on the card, Babu laughs and says go to the capital. "'Maa did'says Chintan Devi.'Maa named. ' Exactly the same is the case with Begumchak's concern Devi of Masauri. When asked her name, she says, "Such a name has been given by the mother that life itself has gone on worrying." Chintan Devi Naam Hai Didi. "Prem Kumar Mani points out that along with calling names, caste-specific surnames are also changing. Prem Kumar Mani says, "Now Gawale people write Yadav, carpenters write Vishwakarma or Sharma, many other castes are changing their names." The prestigious Paris museum, Musée Dorsey, on the left bank of the Seine, was opened in 1986 in an old Boz-Arts railway station and hotel. Aimed at bridging the gap between the Lower Museum and Pongpidu's collections, the museum emphasizes late 19th and 20th century art and houses. It houses the world's largest museum of Impressionist and post-Impressionist paintings. In the late eighties in Bilbao, Spain, when the entire city was being rebuilt, the idea of building a museum developed as a collaboration between Basque authorities and the Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation. The Guggenheim Museum, based on a design by American / Canadian architect Frank Gehry, opened in October 1997. The glass and limestone structure of the building, which stands on the banks of the Navyon river in the old industrial centre of the city, has been cast with titanium. The finished building immediately became popular, with architect Philip Johnson describing it as "the most magnificent building of our time." Brazil's Oscar Niemeyer Museum was opened in 2002-03. It came to be called "The Eye" because it resembles a large human eye placed on a yellow pole. The great Brazilian architect who designed (and gave his name to) it has been an important figure in the Modern Movement. He was 95 when the museum building was completed. The 2000-foot museum displays international artworks as well as Niemeyer's work. The main part of the British Museum in London was designed by architect Robert Smirke in the Neo-Classical style. The inspiration for the huge southern entrance to the museum, which opened in 1852, is taken from ancient Egypt. In 2000, Foster and Partners designed a new Great Court with a magnificent glass ceiling, making the museum's inner courtyard the largest covered complex in Europe. The Royal Ontario Museum of Canada is the largest museum of natural history, art, and culture in the country. It has more than 60 lakh items. The design of Studio Daniel Libeskind's new entrance, along with its original 20th-century building, was described by the museum as "the new distinctive symbol for Toronto in the 21st century." The intricate prismatic aluminium and glass structure built on a steel groove was ranked eighth in the list of'World's Ugliest Buildings'in 2009. Muzio Somaya, in Mexico City, is a private culture institute created in 1994. It is spread over two cities, Plaza Loreto and Plaza Carso. The second was inaugurated in 2011. It was designed by Mexican architect Fernando Romero and designed by Ove Arup and Frank Gehry. Constructed of 16,000 hexagonal aluminium tiles, the museum is 151 feet high and has six floors. It mainly has artefacts from Mexico and Europe. It has the largest collection of Rodin's works outside of France. The Hermitage Museum in St. Petersburg, Russia, is one of the largest and oldest museums in the world. It was inaugurated by Queen Catherine in 1764 and has over three million art and culture exhibits. There are several buildings in the complex of this elaborate government museum. These include the huge green and white Winter Palace, home to former Russian tsarists. The massive palace was designed mainly by Francesco Bartolomeo Rastrelli in the elaborate Baroque style. The Museum of Islamic Art in Doha, the capital of Qatar, was inaugurated in 2008. It was designed by Pritzker Prize-winning architect I.M. Pei, who visited the Arab world for six months at the age of 91 to gain inspiration for the project. The huge five-storeyed limestone building offers a panoramic view of the port of Doha. Its two halves are connected by a large central courtyard. It houses 1400 years of Islamic artifacts. The Museum of Vatican City was inaugurated by Pope Julius II in the 16th century. It has 52 galleries and is one of the largest museums in the world. The museum's collection of religious statues and paintings includes the work of Raphael, Tishian, and Caravaggio. When the original building of Osaka's National Museum of Art was destroyed in 1970, the new building was designed by Cesare Pelli. The main part of the building - including its collection of artefacts - is underground and only the entrance complex is above ground. To make it look more fun, Pelli's studio has created a cane or bamboo-like structure with steel and glass growing along the river. He didn't think he would do any work on breast cancer. Then things changed so much that Mihir's way of working also changed. Her mother-in-law was diagnosed with breast cancer and when the house started talking about it, it was revealed that some other women nearby were also suffering from it. But most of the time, no one likes to talk openly about breast cancer. Sruthi Mihir tried to figure out the problem at home and found out that breast cancer is the most common cancer in women. The earlier the breast cancer is diagnosed, the better, as the longer the delay, the greater the risk of death for the woman. There are no facilities for breast cancer screening in developing countries, especially in rural women. It can be examined with mammography, but requires an expert, while India has only ten thousand radiologists. Given all these realities, Mihir thought of making a machine that was small, could give immediate results, and did not have the risk of radiation. This machine can avoid pain during the examination and can be easily used by a common health worker. In 2009, Mihir, along with co-founder Matthew Kempisi, started UE Life Sciences Inc. in Philadelphia. With an investment and financial support of US $4 million, the work of UE Life Sciences began. Mihir had the experience of taking medical technology "from concept to clinic," while electrical engineer Mathew had the experience of making medical devices. Then UE Life Sciences built a small machine to detect breast cancer. This small device can detect any kind of small lump in the breast and its complete information is available on the digital note pad attached to the machine in a few minutes. "Any medical device is difficult to reach people," Mihir said. You check its success, you have to prepare people for its use first. We want to reach out to women at every level through different delivery agents like NGOs, corporates, health care services, public health centres. "A portable machine test costs less and doesn't cause pain," he says. We want to reach 1 million women in India by the end of 2016. "Says Boman Dhabhar, a renowned cancer specialist from Mumbai," There are many cases where breast cancer has reached an advanced stage. In India, even today, breast cancer is diagnosed first by self-examination, then by expert examination, and mammography at the end. Women do not go to the doctor for a check-up because of hesitation. "With this handy device, nurses or even junior hospital staff can perform a preliminary check-up and suggest mammography if a lump appears," he says. Due to this device, it is not necessary to go to the oncologist for a preliminary examination. We had this device in the breast cancer screening camp detecting lumps in some patients who were later asked for mammography. "In the near future, UE Life Sciences wants to build machines to screen for other types of cancer so that health services can reach the underprivileged in developing countries and raise awareness. After India, UE Life Sciences aspires to work in Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and Latin America. Firecrackers to burn for two hours on Diwali Hindustan has reported on the Supreme Court's order on the burning of crackers. The Supreme Court has ordered the burning of firecrackers for only two hours on Diwali in view of the pollution situation in Delhi. This time will be from 8 pm to 10 pm. It will be the responsibility of the police station in the concerned area to ensure compliance of this order. Violation of the court order will be treated as contempt of court. At the same time, the court said that only green crackers will be made and sold for Diwali. The court has considered only firecrackers with sound and smoke within the prescribed limits to be green crackers. They contain low amounts of nitrogen oxides and sulfur dioxide. It also said that firecrackers should be lit collectively wherever possible in Delhi and NCR. This order will be applicable not only on Diwali but also on any religious and social festival. India first proposed to the United Nations Security Council to designate Masood Azhar as a global terrorist after the 2009 Mumbai attacks. The United States, Britain, and France, the permanent veto-wielding members of the Security Council, later moved a similar resolution, while Russia, another permanent member, has indirectly pledged support for the resolution. Most of the non-permanent members of the Security Council also came out in support of the resolution, leaving China alone as it stood alone for Masood. China has come under fire for supporting the Pakistan-based extremist, whose track record has been very poor. But when the Security Council Sanctions Committee could not reach a consensus on Masood Azhar, France took the lead in declaring him a global terrorist. This further alienated China. Following the February Pulwama terrorist attack in India, France, the United Kingdom, and the United States reintroduced the resolution at a meeting of the UN Sanctions Committee in March. But China put a "technical hold" on it once again at the last minute, and the issue was once again put on hold for six months. This was the fourth time China had imposed a "technical hold" and asked the UN Security Council Sanctions Committee to discuss the issue further. But just days later, China's foreign minister and its ambassador to India began talking about an early resolution of the issue, and within six weeks, China gave its consent to the proposal. Earlier, he used to speak at the closed-door meetings of the sanctions committee, which did not reveal what China actually said in this case. Semabhai's daughter Harmiben says that his maize crop has completely dried up. Semabhai owns two bullocks but they are not being used to plough fields but to dig wells. Semabhai's wife and their daughter are also helping in this work. Last year his crop had dried up and this year his well had also dried up. This is the case with most of the farmers in the Amirgarh block of Palanpur district in north Gujarat. All these fields are dry and there is no water to irrigate the crop. Semabhai lives in Upala Khapa, a small village with no water even for humans and animals. They have land but no water to cultivate. They are forced to work like daily wage labourers. "There is no water in my well, so now I am digging a deep well somewhere," he explains. At first, there was little water in the well but this time due to drought, there is no water even for drinking. "Amirgarh is just 40 kilometers from the district headquarters Palanpur and one has to pass through a dusty road to reach Upala Khapa village. It is a small village, there is a government primary school on the outskirts of the village. As one enters the village, one can see fields on both sides of the road but no greenery in these fields. "Semabhai's family has dug up to 70-80 feet so far but so far there are no signs of getting water. The family has no idea how much digging and digging will still have to be done to get water. Banaskantha District Magistrate Sandeep Sangle says, "Farmers are doing this work on their own. They are not getting any help from the government for this work. "About the growing water crisis in the district, Sandeep says," We are supplying water through pumps and tankers. In the coming days, we will make new plans to tackle the water crisis of Amirgarh and Danta. For this, we are conducting a survey. "I condemn the use of cluster bombs by the Indian Army targeting civilians along the LoC," he wrote. This is a violation of the Geneva Conventions and international law. "Qureshi then followed up with a tweet calling India a regional peacebreaker. He wrote that war-mongering India was not only destabilising regional peace but also committing human rights violations along the Line of Control. In this tweet, Foreign Minister Qureshi has demanded the countries of the world to take note of the recent situation along the Line of Control and Indian-administered Kashmir. Meanwhile, Pakistan Army spokesman Major General Asif Ghafoor has also accused India of violating international agreements. "The use of cluster bombs by the Indian Army is a violation of international agreements and is reprehensible," he tweeted. No weapon can suppress the determination of Kashmiris to achieve their right to self-determination. Kashmir flows in the blood of every Pakistani. The freedom struggle of Kashmiris will be successful. "The Indian Army has denied these allegations by Pakistan. The Indian Army has said that the Pakistan Army constantly promotes militants by infiltrating and arming them. The Indian Army statement further said that the Indian Army always responds to a response and such a response has only been made against military posts of the Pakistan Army and the extremist infiltrators being aided by them. The production and use of cluster bombs are prohibited under the Geneva Accords, but many countries and militaries have been accused of using them in war or armed conflict. These are considered dangerous because many of the small explosives emitted by the main bomb also cause damage around the designated target. This increases the risk of civilian casualties during the conflict. Not only that, small explosives that fall in the vicinity after the main bomb explodes can linger for a long time. In such a situation, even after the conflict is over, there are incidents of loss of life and property due to them. They are used to kill opposing soldiers or damage their vehicles. They can be dropped from fighter jets or launched from the ground. Both India and Pakistan are not party to the treaty. In 2008, an international treaty called the Convention on Cluster Munitions came into existence in Dublin, which proposed a ban on the possession, sale or use of cluster bombs. Signatures began on 3 December 2008, and by September 2018, 108 countries had signed it, while 106 had given in-principle consent to its adoption. However, the treaty was also opposed by several countries, including China, Russia, Israel, and the United States, as well as India and Pakistan. The two countries are yet to sign the treaty. The Citizenship Amendment Act 2019 The central government got the Citizenship Amendment Bill passed by both the houses of Parliament in December 2019. The bill became law after the president signed it. However, since the passage of the bill, protests have been growing and many people have died in the violence in the protests associated with it. The protesters argue that the law is discriminatory on the basis of religion, which is against the basic spirit of the Constitution. The law provides for Indian citizenship to people belonging to six minority communities (Hindu, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi, Christian and Sikh) from Bangladesh, Afghanistan and Pakistan. Earlier, under the Citizenship Act of 1955, people illegally entering India could not get citizenship and there was a provision to send them back to their country or detain them. According to the old law, it was mandatory for a person to have lived in India for at least 11 years to take Indian citizenship. The amended law reduces this time period from 11 to six years for minorities from neighbouring countries. He became the first Indian prime minister to receive this honour. The Order of Zayed is the UAE's highest civilian honour given to monarchs, presidents, and heads of state. According to Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, PM Modi has made significant contributions to enhancing bilateral relations between India and the UAE. In April this year, Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan announced the honour through a tweet. "We have a historic and comprehensive strategic relationship with India, one that my good friend Narendra Modi has contributed greatly to. They have further strengthened these relations. In recognition of his efforts, the President of the UAE, Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan, has conferred on him the Zayed Award. "The Ministry of External Affairs said in a statement that this year's Zayed Award assumes" special significance "as it is being conferred on PM Modi on the occasion of Sheikh Zayed's birth centenary. The year 2019 has been declared the Year of Tolerance in the UAE. The statement further claimed that the UAE is India's third-largest trading partner. The two have a strong bilateral trade relationship and the annual trade between the two is set to reach around $60 billion. Modi's tenure in India and the UAE has seen an unprecedented increase in diplomatic visits between the leaders of the two countries. Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed has visited India twice in the last three years. The first time he visited India was in February 2016, and the second time he attended the Republic Day celebrations in 2017 as the chief guest. Modi, on the other hand, is the first Indian prime minister to visit the UAE twice. He first visited the UAE in August 2015. For the second time in 2018, the UAE invited Narendra Modi as the chief guest at the World Government Summit. This is his third visit in less than five years. During this visit, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met the Crown Prince there. The two countries discussed bilateral, regional and international issues of mutual interest. The Indian Embassy in Abu Dhabi also released a commemorative postage stamp to mark the 150th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi in the presence of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The disease was later named COVID-19, while its virus was called the novel coronavirus. Since then, the disease or infection continued to spread throughout the world. Most countries in the world are currently affected by it and thousands of new cases are being reported every day. He said the global economy has been badly hit by the infection. At the same time, the social structure in the infected countries has also become disorganized. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said, "This pandemic is more than just a health problem. Dealing with this requires a whole of government machinery and a social response, not just one class or community. March 11, 2021: The World Health Organization declares the coronavirus a pandemic. 27 March 2021: UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson tests positive for coronavirus. He was later admitted to the ICU.
